SDIO WiFi probe boot 466.

nodes.name: Circle Project Reference
nodes.summary: R. Stange's Circle bare-metal C++ framework for Raspberry Pi was instrumental in solving the VL805 event ring at boot 143. Circle's xhcieventmanager.cpp and xhcidevice.cpp disassembly revealed three undocumented VL805-specific register write requirements absent from the xHCI spec.

nodes.name: riscos64-clib AArch64 C Library
nodes.summary: RISC OS 64-bit C library used by AArch64 modules. Key integration challenges: _clib_initialisemodule SWI sequence, OS_Module Claim/Free for heap setup, _FORTIFY_SOURCE __vfprintf_chk recursion bug (fixed in boot 432), and GOT-based relocation for disc-loaded modules. Charles Ferguson provides ongoing support.

nodes.name: WIMP Desktop / Task Manager
nodes.summary: Cooperative task scheduler (WIMP) running as the main execution loop. Polls GENET RX ring every 4ms, drives keyboard and mouse input. Boot 413 tri-factor milestone: disc modules loaded, WIMP desktop running, TCP/DNS/DHCP working, keyboard live.

nodes.name: usb_mass_storage.c
nodes.summary: USB Mass Storage class driver implementing Bulk-Only Transport (BOT) over SCSI. Handles device enumeration, READ/WRITE(16) commands, BOT error recovery, read-ahead caching, and blockdev registration with media-class scoring for NVMe/SSD/Flash.

nodes.name: bot_scsi_cmd
nodes.summary: Core BOT SCSI command executor: sends CBW, optional data phase, reads CSW. On data-phase stall issues CLEAR_HALT per BOT §6.6.2 and still drains the CSW to keep the pipe clean. On CSW failure clears both endpoints and calls xhci_ep_recover_guarded.

nodes.name: bot_read_capacity
nodes.summary: Issues SCSI READ CAPACITY (10) command via bot_scsi_cmd and parses the 8-byte response to extract the last LBA and block size for a given LUN.

nodes.name: bot_read_capacity16
nodes.summary: Issues SCSI READ CAPACITY (16) for drives >2 TB: builds a 16-byte CDB, parses the 32-byte response, extracts 64-bit last LBA and 32-bit block size. Handles RTL9210 bridge quirks.

nodes.name: usb_bot_rw
nodes.summary: Issues READ(16) or WRITE(16) SCSI commands over BOT using 64-bit LBA. Switched from READ(10) to avoid RTL9210 bridge firmware bug that silently returns zeros for certain LBA ranges.

nodes.name: bot_recover
nodes.summary: Full BOT error recovery: BOT Mass Storage Reset, CLEAR_HALT on bulk IN+OUT, xhci_ep_recover_guarded (CLEAR_HALT preceded), then TUR retry up to 5 times.

nodes.name: usb_bdev_read
nodes.summary: blockdev read callback implementing an 8-sector (4 KB) read-ahead cache. On cache miss fetches READAHEAD_N sectors; detects RTL9210 zero-return bug and retries after 2 ms.

nodes.name: usb_bdev_write
nodes.summary: blockdev write callback: invalidates read-ahead cache then issues a WRITE(16) via usb_bot_rw.

nodes.name: usb_storage_probe
nodes.summary: MSC probe: declines UAS, allocates usb_storage_t, finds bulk endpoints, performs BOT reset + CLEAR_HALT + TUR retry loop + INQUIRY + READ CAPACITY (RC10 then RC16 polling), registers blockdev with media-class classification.

nodes.name: usb_mass_storage_init
nodes.summary: Registers the USB MSC class driver with the USB core.

nodes.name: timer.c
nodes.summary: ARM Generic Timer driver for Phoenix OS. Manages per-CPU timer lists with spinlock protection, reads CNTPCT_EL0/CNTFRQ_EL0 system registers for time-keeping, and implements a 4 ms (250 Hz) PPI-30 interrupt via timer_enable_interrupt(). The ISR (timer_irq_handler) re-arms the countdown and sets deferred HID request flags (hid_mouse_request, hid_kbd_request) consumed by wimp_task(). timer_tick() walks expired callbacks and calls schedule().

nodes.name: timer_init
nodes.summary: Global timer initialization. Zeroes all per-CPU timer lists and initializes all MAX_CPUS spinlocks. Logs the ARM generic timer frequency read from CNTFRQ_EL0.

nodes.name: timer_init_cpu
nodes.summary: Per-CPU timer initialization. Resets the timer list for the current CPU, initializes its spinlock, and sets CNTP_CTL_EL0 = 0x2 (IMASK=1, ENABLE=0) to keep the timer masked until irq_init() completes.

nodes.name: timer_enable_interrupt
nodes.summary: Arms the ARM generic timer at 4 ms (250 Hz). Registers timer_irq_handler on GIC PPI 30 (nCNTPNSIRQ) via irq_set_handler/irq_unmask, loads CNTP_TVAL_EL0 with the computed tick count, and sets CNTP_CTL_EL0 = 1 (ENABLE=1, IMASK=0). Must be called after irq_init() and after DAIF.I is cleared.

nodes.name: timer_tick
nodes.summary: Software timer tick dispatcher. Walks the per-CPU expired timer list under spinlock, fires each callback, then calls schedule() and re-arms the hardware countdown register.

nodes.name: timer_irq_handler
nodes.summary: GIC PPI-30 interrupt service routine for the ARM generic timer. Re-arms CNTP_TVAL_EL0 immediately, then sets hid_mouse_request=1 every tick and hid_kbd_request=1 every 4th tick for deferred HID polling in wimp_task().

nodes.name: dashboard.yml
nodes.summary: GitHub Actions workflow that builds and deploys the Phoenix OS knowledge dashboard to GitHub Pages. Triggers on push to main and on workflow_dispatch. Uses actions/checkout and actions/deploy-pages to publish static dashboard content from the repository.

nodes.name: README_BOOT.md
nodes.summary: Boot guide for Phoenix OS at boot438. Describes SD card file requirements (kernel8.img, config.txt, Pi 4 firmware blobs), hardware setup (serial console GPIO 14/15 at 115200 8N1, NVMe via USB-C DeskPi Pro). Documents expected 10-step boot sequence including GPU framebuffer, device tree, MMU, scheduler, heap, GIC, PCIe/USB, VFS/modules/network. Lists module status table (AArch64 modules all init OK, ARM32 modules deferred). Tracks boot arc history from boot431 to boot438 with fix summaries. Includes troubleshooting guide.

nodes.name: ARCHITECTURE.md
nodes.summary: Architecture overview for Phoenix OS. Describes target hardware (Raspberry Pi 4B BCM2711 Cortex-A72, secondary Pi 5 BCM2712). Documents the design philosophy: bare-metal AArch64 kernel inspired by RISC OS, single-address-space, cooperative-first, all drivers/kernel/apps run at EL1, monolithic image. Defines the memory map: 0x00000000-0xFFFF reserved/MMIO trap, 0x00010000-0x1FFFF xHCI DMA buffer (Normal-NC), 0x00080000 kernel load address, 0x00100000+ kernel heap. References the xHCI DMA sub-layout (DCBAA, command ring, event ring, ERST, MSI pad).

nodes.name: USB_XHCI_VL805.md
nodes.summary: Detailed development history and breadcrumb document for the VL805 xHCI USB driver. Documents hardware topology (BCM2711 PCIe RC → VL805, BDF 01:00.0, PCI ID 1106:3483), VL805 MCU 8051 firmware boot behaviour, initialisation sequence (PCIe bring-up, ring setup, controller start, port power, port scan/enumeration), the force-ring pattern (atomic W1C→RS→CRCR→doorbell within 4ms MCU window), PP power-cycle port recovery, companion port DR=1 hazard, and the event ring write-back problem (diagnosed at boot61, root causes listed). Key learnings indexed by boot number (boots 1-61). Documented at boot61 milestone when USB-MSC class driver first binds.

nodes.name: milestone-usb-mass-storage-bot.md
nodes.summary: Milestone document for USB Bulk-Only Transport (BOT) mass storage driver, achieved at boot163. Documents the hardware (Pi 4B DeskPi Pro, VL805 xHCI, VL812 hub, ASMedia ASM1153E SATA bridge, 500GB SSD registering as usb0). Details code changes: xhci_configure_endpoints() for ConfigureEndpoint command, xhci_bulk_transfer() full implementation with DMA bounce buffer and doorbell, SET_CONFIGURATION control transfer (boot162 fix), usb_mass_storage.c rewrite with bot_scsi_cmd()/bot_read_capacity(), blockdev_ops_t registration. Documents DMA memory layout for per-slot bulk rings. Bug timeline from boot159-163. Next steps: FileCore sector reads, partition table parsing, Makefile -MMD dependency tracking.

nodes.name: usb_gadget_start
nodes.summary: Enables the DWC2 D+ pull-up to signal device presence to the host.

nodes.name: aif.h
nodes.summary: Public header for the Phoenix RISC OS AIF loader. Documents the AIF header layout (offsets 0x00–0x100+) as defined by riscos64-clib's aif.lnk linker script, the application memory slot layout (base 0x8000, top 0x30000000), and declares the single public function aif_run. Include guard: AIF_H.

nodes.name: aif_run
nodes.summary: Declaration: int aif_run(const char *path, const char *cmdtail). Loads and executes an AIF absolute file from the RISC OS filing system. path is a RISC OS pathname (e.g. '$.!Boot.Resources.!OBSD.BASIC'); cmdtail is the command tail passed to the application (may be empty string). Returns 0 on normal application exit, -1 on load error. May not return if the application calls OS_Exit directly.

nodes.name: LICENSE
nodes.summary: MIT licence text granting broad permission to use, copy, modify, and distribute the Phoenix OS source code.

nodes.name: NOTES.md
nodes.summary: Working notes on integrating the RISC OS SystemVars module into Phoenix OS, documenting the reversed 'kernel collusion' mechanism, the default variable namespace established by SystemVarsDefaults, the Phoenix wiring plan, and open questions requiring further reverse-engineering.

nodes.name: swi_call.S
nodes.summary: AArch64 assembly veneer implementing _kernel_call, the calling convention used by OS_ClaimOSSWI-registered handlers; marshals up to 10 32-bit registers (R0-R9) from an inregs array, calls the handler with the private word in x12, captures outregs, and returns an error pointer.
nodes.languageNotes: Also contains test_osswi_handler, a self-test stub that computes R0+R1 and clears V to verify the register/private-word passing convention end-to-end. The calling convention (V flag for error signalling, x12 for private word) mirrors the 32-bit RISC OS module ABI.

nodes.name: _kernel_call
nodes.summary: Loads R0-R9 from an optional inregs uint32_t array into w0-w9, passes the private word in x12, calls an OS_ClaimOSSWI handler via blr, then stores the resulting registers to an optional outregs array; returns the error pointer (x0 if V was set, else 0).

nodes.name: test_osswi_handler
nodes.summary: Self-test handler stub: sets R0 = R0+R1 and R2 = private word, then clears all condition flags to signal no error; used by osswi_selftest to validate _kernel_call.

nodes.name: Objects.c
nodes.summary: Implements FileCore object I/O — loading and saving disc objects via their Sector Index Numbers (SINs) — handling fragmented objects through the map and supporting copy, extract, and statistics operations.
nodes.languageNotes: SIN-to-disc-address translation goes through SinAddr/MapAddr, mirroring the FileCore map indirection layer; CopyObject uses RISC OS OSFile/OSGBPB SWI wrappers for host-side extraction.

nodes.name: ReadObjects
nodes.summary: Recursively enumerates all FileCore objects starting from a given SIN, reading directories and accumulating object statistics across the disc image.

nodes.name: SinAddr
nodes.summary: Translates a FileCore Sector Index Number (SIN) to a physical disc address by walking the allocation map, handling both direct and indirect map entries.

nodes.name: LoadObject
nodes.summary: Loads a FileCore object identified by its SIN into a caller-supplied buffer, handling fragmented objects by reading each contiguous run of sectors via SinAddr.

nodes.name: SaveObject
nodes.summary: Writes a FileCore object from a caller-supplied buffer back to disc at the physical sectors identified by its SIN, handling fragmented extents.

nodes.name: AddObjectStat
nodes.summary: Accumulates global file and directory count/size statistics as objects are enumerated during a disc-image scan.

nodes.name: dr_api.h
nodes.summary: Public C header exposing the discreader module API — function declarations and shared types that consumers (e.g., the filing-system layer) use to initialise, query, and write FileCore disc images.
nodes.languageNotes: Header-only interface with no implementations; guards the public surface of the discreader module from internal implementation details.

nodes.name: vfs.h
nodes.summary: VFS (Virtual Filesystem) header defining the shared filesystem abstraction types, vfs_open/close/read/seek/write function prototypes, and the vfs_handle structure used across the kernel filing layer.

nodes.name: sched.c
nodes.summary: Implements a 4-CPU symmetric round-robin scheduler with per-CPU run queues, idle tasks, spinlock-protected enqueue/dequeue, assembly-level context switching, and cross-CPU task wakeup via inter-processor interrupts.
nodes.languageNotes: context_switch relies on inline assembly or an assembly stub to save/restore AArch64 callee-saved registers; the scheduler uses __builtin_ctzll for efficient least-loaded CPU selection.

nodes.name: sched_init
nodes.summary: Initializes the global scheduler data structures and spinlock before any CPU-specific setup is performed.

nodes.name: sched_init_cpu
nodes.summary: Sets up the per-CPU run queue and creates the CPU's idle task, enrolling it in the scheduler so the CPU always has something to run.

nodes.name: context_switch
nodes.summary: Performs the low-level AArch64 context switch between two tasks, saving the outgoing task's register state and restoring the incoming task's state.

nodes.name: schedule
nodes.summary: Core scheduler dispatch function: acquires the per-CPU run queue lock, selects the next runnable task via pick_next_task, and calls context_switch to transfer execution.

nodes.name: task_block
nodes.summary: Marks the current task as blocked with the given state and immediately yields the CPU by calling schedule.

nodes.name: task_wakeup
nodes.summary: Transitions a blocked task back to the runnable state and sends an inter-processor interrupt to wake the target CPU if the task belongs to a different core.

nodes.name: enqueue_task
nodes.summary: Appends a task to a scheduler run queue under spinlock protection, ensuring safe concurrent access from multiple CPUs.

nodes.name: yield
nodes.summary: Thin wrapper that voluntarily surrenders the CPU by calling schedule, allowing other runnable tasks to execute.

nodes.name: .gitignore
nodes.summary: Git ignore rules excluding build artifacts, object files, kernel ELF binaries, and editor temporaries from version control.

nodes.name: WORKFLOW.md
nodes.summary: Developer session guide covering project vision and aims, current status at boot577, hardware setup, FileCore parameters, SBPr directory format, multi-disc priority rules, milestone history, next steps, and important gotchas for ongoing development.

nodes.name: HAL_PLAN.md
nodes.summary: Architectural planning document for a Device-Tree-driven Hardware Abstraction Layer, covering the target architecture, existing dt-hal-unified branch work, quirk registry design for per-model behaviour, incremental implementation phases, and open risks for supporting multiple Raspberry Pi board variants.

nodes.name: PI5_FACTS.md
nodes.summary: Hardware fact table for the BCM2712-based Raspberry Pi 5, recording confirmed address maps, SoC peripheral window, RP1 southbridge PCIe endpoint identity, DMA coherency behaviour, and gaps identified from real Pi OS boot-log observations to guide the Pi 5 port.

nodes.name: PI5_PORT_PLAN.md
nodes.summary: Detailed nine-phase implementation plan for porting Phoenix OS to the Raspberry Pi 5 (BCM2712), covering a code audit, DT-first peripheral detection, GIC bring-up, mailbox, SD/FileCore, PCIe RC and RP1 southbridge, USB via RP1 xHCI, Ethernet GEM driver, NVMe, SMP polish, and a risk register.

nodes.name: mmc.c
nodes.summary: SD/MMC block device driver using the SDHCI register interface, implementing card initialisation, chunked multi-block read/write with AutoCMD12, and registration with the OS block-device layer.
nodes.languageNotes: Polled SDHCI driver with no interrupt handling; uses MMIO_READ/MMIO_WRITE macros for memory-mapped register access and a custom mmc_time_ms timestamp for timeout loops.

nodes.name: mmc.h
nodes.summary: Public header for the MMC/SD driver, declaring the mmc_init, mmc_read_blocks, mmc_write_blocks, and mmc_get_info entry points together with any shared type definitions.

nodes.name: usb_dwc2.c
nodes.summary: Full DWC2 USB 2.0 OTG host-mode driver covering core reset, host-mode init, port power/reset, channel-based DMA transfers with split-transaction support for FS/LS devices behind hubs, USB enumeration, HID device polling for keyboard and mouse, and a scan-ports entry point for periodic device detection.
nodes.languageNotes: Implements split transactions (HCSPLT) manually in software to support low/full-speed devices behind USB hubs; uses explicit D-cache clean/invalidate operations around DMA buffers to maintain coherency on AArch64.

nodes.name: sdhci_wait_cmd_ready
nodes.summary: Polls the SDHCI status register until the command-inhibit bit clears, providing a synchronisation barrier before issuing a new SD command.

nodes.name: sdhci_wait_data_ready
nodes.summary: Polls the SDHCI status register until the data-inhibit bit clears, ensuring the data lines are free before beginning a data transfer.

nodes.name: mmc_send_cmd
nodes.summary: Core SDHCI command-dispatch routine that programs the argument, transfer mode, block count, and command registers, then polls for completion and reads back the response and error status.

nodes.name: sdhci_reset
nodes.summary: Issues a software reset to the SDHCI controller and waits for the reset to complete before returning.

nodes.name: mmc_bd_read
nodes.summary: Block-device callback adapter that forwards read requests from the OS block-device layer to mmc_read_blocks.

nodes.name: mmc_bd_write
nodes.summary: Block-device callback adapter that forwards write requests from the OS block-device layer to mmc_write_blocks.

nodes.name: mmc_init
nodes.summary: Performs full SD card initialisation: resets the controller, negotiates voltage and bus width, executes the SD initialisation command sequence (CMD0/CMD8/ACMD41/CMD2/CMD3/CMD7/CMD6), reads the CSD to determine card capacity, and registers the device with the block-device layer.

nodes.name: mmc_read_chunk
nodes.summary: Reads up to one DMA-aligned chunk of blocks from the SD card using CMD18 (READ_MULTIPLE_BLOCK) with FIFO polling and AutoCMD12 stop-transmission.

nodes.name: mmc_read_blocks
nodes.summary: Public exported entry point that splits a large multi-block read into successive mmc_read_chunk calls to stay within hardware transfer limits.

nodes.name: mmc_write_chunk
nodes.summary: Writes a single DMA-aligned chunk of blocks to the SD card using CMD25 (WRITE_MULTIPLE_BLOCK) with FIFO polling and AutoCMD12 stop-transmission.

nodes.name: mmc_write_blocks
nodes.summary: Public exported entry point that splits a large multi-block write into successive mmc_write_chunk calls to stay within hardware transfer limits.

nodes.name: mmc_get_info
nodes.summary: Exported function that fills a caller-supplied info structure with the MMC device block size and total block count.

nodes.name: dcache_clean
nodes.summary: Flushes a range of virtual addresses from the D-cache to main memory using AArch64 DC CVAC instructions, ensuring DMA output buffers are coherent before the hardware reads them.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses inline AArch64 assembly cache-maintenance instructions in a cache-line-aligned loop.

nodes.name: dcache_inval
nodes.summary: Invalidates a range of D-cache lines using AArch64 DC IVAC instructions so that subsequent CPU reads see fresh DMA-delivered data.
nodes.languageNotes: Pairs with dcache_clean; together they provide the manual cache coherency required when the DWC2 performs bus-master DMA.

nodes.name: dwc2_core_reset
nodes.summary: Performs a full software reset of the DWC2 core, waiting for AHB idle and reset-complete conditions before returning, with timeout diagnostics.

nodes.name: dwc2_core_init_host
nodes.summary: Configures the DWC2 core for USB host mode: sets ULPI/PHY mode, programs FIFO sizes, flushes TX FIFOs, enables DMA, and unmasks host-channel interrupts.

nodes.name: dwc2_port_power_on
nodes.summary: Enables port power on the DWC2 host port and waits for the power-stable delay before reading the port status.

nodes.name: dwc2_port_reset_and_enable
nodes.summary: Issues a USB port reset pulse, waits for the port to complete reset and enable itself, then reads the resulting port speed.

nodes.name: dwc2_chan_go
nodes.summary: Arms a DWC2 host channel with the given HCCHAR, HCTSIZ, DMA address, and HCSPLT values, enables the channel, and polls HCINT for transfer completion.

nodes.name: dwc2_split_one
nodes.summary: Executes a single split transaction consisting of a Start Split phase followed by a Complete Split phase, used to transfer data to/from full/low-speed devices connected via a hub.

nodes.name: dwc2_hc_xfer_split
nodes.summary: Handles a complete split-mode host-channel transfer loop, breaking data into FS/LS MTU packets and issuing successive split transactions until the requested byte count is satisfied.

nodes.name: dwc2_hc_xfer
nodes.summary: Top-level host-channel transfer function that selects between split-mode (for FS/LS behind hubs) and direct high-speed channel transfers, managing multi-packet chunking and retry on NAK/NYET.

nodes.name: dwc2_ctrl_xfer
nodes.summary: Executes a complete USB control transfer (SETUP plus optional DATA plus STATUS stages), applying D-cache maintenance on the data buffer and driving each stage through dwc2_hc_xfer.

nodes.name: dwc2_enumerate_device
nodes.summary: Enumerates a newly attached USB device at address 0: reads the device descriptor to determine class/subclass, assigns a USB address, and returns the device maximum packet size and class information.

nodes.name: dwc2_hub_get_port_status
nodes.summary: Issues a GetPortStatus class request to a USB hub and unpacks the resulting wPortStatus and wPortChange words into separate output pointers.

nodes.name: dwc2_parse_hid_ifaces
nodes.summary: Walks a USB configuration descriptor to find all HID interfaces, extracting interface numbers, HID protocol codes, interrupt-IN endpoint addresses, and max-packet-sizes for subsequent polling.

nodes.name: dwc2_enum_child
nodes.summary: Fully enumerates a USB device connected behind a hub: reads descriptors, assigns address, selects active configuration, sets HID boot protocol, and registers discovered HID endpoints for polling.

nodes.name: dwc2_enum_hub
nodes.summary: Enumerates a USB hub: configures it, reads the hub descriptor, powers each port, waits for device-connect events, and recursively enumerates any child devices discovered on hub ports.

nodes.name: dwc2_proc_mouse
nodes.summary: Decodes a HID mouse report and delivers button and relative movement deltas to the OS via mouse_event, translating raw USB HID data into OS pointer events.

nodes.name: dwc2_proc_keyboard
nodes.summary: Decodes a HID keyboard report, translates USB HID key codes to OS scan codes applying modifier state, and delivers key-down/key-up events via keyboard_event.

nodes.name: dwc2_int_in_once
nodes.summary: Performs a single interrupt-IN transaction on a HID endpoint, handling split transactions for LS devices and copying the received data into the caller buffer.

nodes.name: dwc2_hid_poll
nodes.summary: Exported polling function that reads pending HID reports from all registered keyboard and mouse endpoints and dispatches them to their respective event processors.

nodes.name: dwc2_init
nodes.summary: Exported initialisation function that maps the DWC2 peripheral base address, resets the core, configures it as a host, powers the port, waits for device connect, and issues a port reset to bring the bus to an operational state.

nodes.name: dwc2_device_present
nodes.summary: Exported predicate that returns non-zero if a USB device is currently detected on the DWC2 host port.

nodes.name: dwc2_start
nodes.summary: Exported start routine that initialises the DWC2 host, detects the speed and class of the connected device, and performs full USB enumeration for a direct device or for a hub with downstream child devices.

nodes.name: dwc2_scan_ports
nodes.summary: Exported entry point called periodically to attempt USB device start and enumeration by delegating to dwc2_start.

nodes.name: dt_diag.c
nodes.summary: Device tree diagnostics module that prints a structured dump of the parsed FDT — board compatibility strings, memory ranges, CPU list, and GIC addresses — via the kernel debug channel.

nodes.name: dt_dump_diag
nodes.summary: Walks the raw FDT and the parsed dt_state struct to print board compatibility, memory, CPU, and GIC details to the kernel debug output.

nodes.name: fdt_walk.c
nodes.summary: Low-level Flattened Device Tree parser implementing big-endian token walking, node traversal, property lookup, cell-width-aware register reads, and compatible-string matching over a raw FDT blob in memory.
nodes.languageNotes: All FDT integers are big-endian; be32() performs a manual byte-reversal since the kernel has no libc. Node handles are opaque uint32_t offsets into the struct block, not pointers.

nodes.name: fdt_find_node
nodes.summary: Walks the FDT struct block following a slash-delimited path string to locate and return the handle of the named node.

nodes.name: fdt_get_property
nodes.summary: Scans a node's property tokens to find one matching the given name, returning a pointer and length to the raw property value.

nodes.name: fdt_is_compatible
nodes.summary: Searches the null-separated compatible string list in a node's compatible property for an exact match against the given string.

nodes.name: fdt_next_compatible
nodes.summary: Iterates the entire FDT struct block searching for the next node that has a matching compatible string, enabling device enumeration.

nodes.name: fdt_read_reg
nodes.summary: Reads a node's reg property respecting parent #address-cells and #size-cells widths, returning base address and size as 64-bit values.

nodes.name: skip_node
nodes.summary: Advances the struct-block offset past an entire FDT node and all its nested children and properties, used internally by sibling traversal.

nodes.name: fdt_root
nodes.summary: Returns a node handle for the FDT root node by locating the first FDT_BEGIN_NODE token in the struct block.

nodes.name: fdt_check
nodes.summary: Validates the FDT magic number (0xD00DFEED) and returns true if the blob is a well-formed FDT.

nodes.name: fdt_first_child
nodes.summary: Finds and returns the handle of the first child node of a given parent by scanning past the parent's properties to the first nested FDT_BEGIN_NODE.

nodes.name: fdt_next_sibling
nodes.summary: Returns the next sibling node of a given node by skipping the current node's subtree and finding the following FDT_BEGIN_NODE token.

nodes.name: fdt_walk.h
nodes.summary: Public API header for the FDT walker, declaring all fdt_* function prototypes, the fdt_node handle type, the fdt_prop struct, and FDT token constants used across the kernel device tree layer.

nodes.name: malloc.c
nodes.summary: Kernel heap allocator providing kmalloc, kfree, and kcalloc over a 128 MB static heap, using a first-fit free-list with bidirectional physical block links, block-split/coalesce, and header/tail-canary corruption detection.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses magic words (HDR_MAGIC=0xFEEDC0DE, TAIL_MAGIC=0xDEADC0DE) at each block's header and tail to detect corruption and double-free at kfree time without requiring a separate debug build; 16-byte alignment enforced throughout.

nodes.name: kmalloc
nodes.summary: Allocates at least `size` bytes from the kernel heap using first-fit search, optionally splits the found block to reduce waste, plants a tail canary, and returns a 16-byte-aligned pointer.

nodes.name: kfree
nodes.summary: Returns a block to the kernel heap free-list, validating the header magic and tail canary for corruption/double-free detection, then coalesces adjacent free blocks.

nodes.name: kcalloc
nodes.summary: Allocates and zeroes nmemb * size bytes, with overflow-safe total size computation, delegating to kmalloc.

nodes.name: malloc_init
nodes.summary: Initialises the heap by placing a single free block header covering the entire 128 MB heap region and setting the free-list head.

nodes.name: coalesce_forward
nodes.summary: Merges a just-freed block with its physically adjacent successor block if that successor is also free, reducing heap fragmentation.

nodes.name: heap_stats
nodes.summary: Prints heap utilisation diagnostics: bytes allocated, total heap size, free bytes, and number of free blocks.

nodes.name: DiscReader.h
nodes.summary: Master header for the RISC OS-style DiscReader subsystem, defining all ADFS on-disc data structures (DiscRecord, directory layouts, map zone constants) and declaring the public API for every DiscReader submodule including DiscOps, Directories, DirUtils, Map, and Objects.
nodes.languageNotes: Defines both old-style Hugo/Nick (E-format) and new BigDir (E+ format) directory layouts. The DR_DIRBUF macro rounds directory allocations up to the native sector size, which was the key fix for 4K NVMe sector support.

nodes.name: Directories.c
nodes.summary: Implements recursive ADFS directory sector parsing, reading both old Hugo/Nick (E-format) and new BigDir (E+ format) directory structures, verifying each entry against the object map and recursing into subdirectories.

nodes.name: DiscOps.c
nodes.summary: Phoenix bare-metal I/O layer for DiscReader, replacing RISC OS SWI disc access with calls to the Phoenix block device interface and providing 4K-native NVMe sector translation via a temporary buffer to avoid buffer overruns on sub-sector reads.
nodes.languageNotes: The ReadSectors function detects when the requested byte count is not a whole multiple of the native sector size (e.g. 512-byte boot block on a 4K-native NVMe) and reads into a temporary heap buffer before copying out exactly the requested bytes. This was the critical fix enabling all 14 disc modules to load from the Crucial P3 500GB.

nodes.name: DirUtils.c
nodes.summary: ADFS directory utility functions including entry lookup, load/save, name comparison using a 256-entry RISC OS collation table, and byte-field accessors (GetI/SetI/GetS/SetS); write-path functions (CreateDir, RemoveEntry, SortDirectory) are conditionally disabled with #if 0 for the read-only bare-metal Phoenix port.
nodes.languageNotes: The 256-entry fn_collate table implements the RISC OS filer collation order (case-insensitive, locale-aware character ordering) for filename_cmp. Most write-path functions are compiled out with #if 0 since the Phoenix port is currently read-only; AddEntry and AdjustNameHeap are re-enabled for new-file creation (Stage C).

nodes.name: ReadDirectory
nodes.summary: Recursively reads an ADFS directory by loading its sector data, branching on filecore version to handle old-style (Hugo/Nick) and new BigDir (E+) layouts, and iterating over all entries via ReadEntry.

nodes.name: ReadEntry
nodes.summary: Parses a single ADFS directory entry in either old or new format, extracts name/SIN/size/attributes, validates the SIN against the object map, and dispatches to ReadSharedObject, ReadNonSharedObject, or ReadSubDir as appropriate.

nodes.name: ReadNonSharedObject
nodes.summary: Accumulates allocation size for a non-shared ADFS map object by walking its chunk list, detecting excess fragments and fragmentation statistics.

nodes.name: ReadSectors
nodes.summary: Translates a logical ADFS sector read into a Phoenix block-device read, handling 4K-native NVMe sectors by reading into a temporary buffer when the requested byte count is not a whole multiple of the native block size.

nodes.name: ReadBytes
nodes.summary: Byte-addressed disc read that converts byte offsets to sector numbers accounting for the partition LBA base, using a temporary buffer for unaligned spans.

nodes.name: WriteSectors
nodes.summary: Translates a logical ADFS sector write to the Phoenix block device; logs non-SD writes for visibility but allows them, with the NVMe PCIe device naturally protected by its unregistered write stub.

nodes.name: LoadDirectory
nodes.summary: Loads an ADFS directory from disc into a heap buffer, handling both old and new format including multi-extension BigDir reallocation up to DIRECTORY_MAX_SIZE.

nodes.name: IsDirectory
nodes.summary: Loads a disc object and validates its header magic (Hugo/Nick for E-format, SBPr/oven for BigDir) to determine whether the object at a given SIN is a directory, returning the parent SIN and directory name.

nodes.name: AddEntry
nodes.summary: Inserts a new entry into an ADFS directory in collated order, supporting both old E-format (fixed-size entries) and new E+ BigDir (variable-length name heap), with automatic directory extension for BigDir up to 4 MB.

nodes.name: AdjustNameHeap
nodes.summary: Adjusts the BigDir name heap by shifting entries and updating all name pointer fields when entries are inserted or removed.

nodes.name: FindEntry
nodes.summary: Searches an in-memory directory for a named entry using RISC OS collation order, returning the SIN or zero if not found.

nodes.name: GetI
nodes.summary: Reads a 1-4 byte little-endian integer from an unaligned byte offset in a disc buffer.

nodes.name: SetI
nodes.summary: Writes a 1-4 byte little-endian integer to an unaligned byte offset in a disc buffer.

nodes.name: GetS
nodes.summary: Reads a control-character-terminated or fixed-length ASCII string from a disc buffer, converting the RISC OS control-character terminator to a C null terminator.

nodes.name: filename_cmp
nodes.summary: Compares two ADFS filenames using the 256-entry RISC OS filer collation table (case-insensitive, extended-ASCII-aware), returning negative/zero/positive like strcmp.

nodes.name: dr_init.c
nodes.summary: Phoenix OS DiscReader initialization and public API glue layer. Exposes dr_init, dr_find_in_dir, dr_create_file, dr_save_object, dr_read_disc_name, dr_shutdown, and related helpers that filecore.c and other callers use to mount ADFS new-map discs and access files by SIN.
nodes.languageNotes: Pure C with bare-metal AArch64 conventions; uses kmalloc/kfree rather than libc malloc; ROR macro for 32-bit rotate used in the checkbyte algorithm.

nodes.name: dr_init
nodes.summary: Initializes the DiscReader for a given block device and LBA base: sets I/O globals, zeroes the s_info structure, then calls Initialise, ReadBootBlock, and ReadMap to load the entire ADFS zone map into RAM.

nodes.name: dr_update_entry_len
nodes.summary: Updates an existing directory entry's length, load address, and exec address in its parent directory, recomputes the FileCore-compatible check-byte, and writes the directory back via SaveObject. Handles both normal (Hugo/Nick) and big (SBPr/oven) directory formats.

nodes.name: dr_create_file
nodes.summary: Creates a new small file within an existing parent directory's shared fragment by finding a free slice run, inserting a directory entry via AddEntry, recomputing the check-byte, and writing the updated directory back. Returns the new SIN in out_sin.

nodes.name: dr_dump_alloc_params
nodes.summary: Diagnostic helper that prints the bound disc's allocation model parameters (idlen, log2bpmb, LFAU, nzones, free count, share size) and decodes the root fragment's chunk and slice layout to aid new-file allocation design.

nodes.name: dr_read_disc_name
nodes.summary: Lightweight disc-name probe for use during boot scanning: reads only the 4K boot block and the single map sector containing the disc record, then extracts the disc name without allocating the full zone map. Temporarily retargets DiscReader I/O globals and restores them on return.

nodes.name: dr_find_in_dir
nodes.summary: Loads an ADFS directory by SIN and performs a case-insensitive name search, returning the found entry's SIN, size, and directory flag. Handles both normal and big directory formats; records load/exec words in dr_last_load/dr_last_exec for callers that need RISC OS filetype.

nodes.name: dr_object_size
nodes.summary: Walks the LFAU chain for a given SIN and returns the total allocated bytes, rounded up to an LFAU boundary (bpmb = 1 << log2bpmb).

nodes.name: dr_shutdown
nodes.summary: Frees all DiscReader in-memory state: zone map buffers, per-object chunk/shared lists, free-fragment list, and I/O globals. Must be called on unmount or disc rebind.

nodes.name: dr_dir_checkbyte
nodes.summary: Static helper that replicates FileCore's directory check-byte algorithm (ROR-13 XOR fold) for both normal and big directory formats. Must match FileCore exactly or the directory becomes unreadable.

nodes.name: BTSdioTypeA
nodes.summary: Main body of the BTSdioTypeA RISC OS C module: implements the CYW43455 Bluetooth-over-SDIO (func3, Type-A) driver for Phoenix OS, providing probe, firmware download, polled HCI RX, and the CMHG Init/Final entry points that register/deregister with the kernel SDIODriver SWI provider.
nodes.languageNotes: RISC OS C module using no .c extension (RISC OS directory convention c/FileName). AArch64-clean: all pointer-to-register casts use intptr_t. SWI calls via _kernel_swi/_swix. CMHG-generated module header supplies the Init/Final entry points.

nodes.name: bt_download_firmware
nodes.summary: Reads a binary BCM .hcd firmware patch from disc via OS_GBPB, walks its [opcode:2][plen:1][data] records, H4-wraps each as an HCI command (type 0x01), and sends them to the CYW43455 over SDIO func3 WriteBytes.

nodes.name: bt_irq
nodes.summary: Polled IRQ handler called from the WIMP loop; drains up to 16 Type-A RX frames from func3, parsing HCI event packets (type 0x04) and buffering all received data into the RX ring.

nodes.name: bt_wait_event
nodes.summary: Synchronously polls func3 for a single HCI event response, used during bring-up milestones (HCI Reset, Read Local BD_ADDR) before the polled RX loop is running.

nodes.name: bt_probe
nodes.summary: SDIO driver probe callback: allocates bt_priv state, enables func3, claims the polled IRQ, downloads the .hcd firmware, then executes the Phoenix milestone sequence (HCI Reset + Read Local BD_ADDR) and prints the Bluetooth MAC address.

nodes.name: Init
nodes.summary: CMHG module initialisation entry point: allocates RX and log ring buffers, then calls SDIODriver_RegisterDriver SWI to register the bt_id_table/bt_probe driver with the kernel SDIO provider.

nodes.name: Final
nodes.summary: CMHG module finalisation entry point: deregisters the driver from the kernel SDIO provider via SDIODriver_DeregisterDriver SWI.

nodes.name: SDIODriver
nodes.summary: Client-side ABI header for the Phoenix SDIODriver SWI provider (chunk 0x59000): defines the seven SWI numbers, the sdio_device_id, sdio_func, and sdio_driver structs that must match the kernel provider's layout byte-for-byte on AArch64.
nodes.languageNotes: 64-bit clean: sdio_driver carries function pointers as 8-byte fields on AArch64. This header mirrors drivers/sdio/sdiodriver.h in the Phoenix kernel; both sides must agree on struct layout across the SWI boundary.

nodes.name: BTSdioTypeAHdr
nodes.summary: CMunge (CMHG) module header declaring the BTSdioTypeA 64-bit RISC OS module entry table: specifies the module title, help string, and Init/Final as the only entry points (no start code, as 64-bit modules do not support it).
nodes.languageNotes: Processed by CMunge -64bit; comments go through the C preprocessor so apostrophes are forbidden. No module-is-runnable directive because CMunge -64bit has no 64-bit start code implementation.

nodes.name: .robuild.yaml
nodes.summary: build.riscos.online job descriptor for BTSdioTypeA: configures the aarch64 environment, sets RISC OS library paths, and runs riscos64-amu with BUILD64=1 to produce the rm64 AArch64 module artifact — though in practice AArch64 dispatch on the remote service is non-functional and local Docker builds are required.
nodes.languageNotes: The aarch64 environment on build.riscos.online currently lacks real AArch64 tools (as of Jun 2025); this file serves as reference only — local gerph/riscos-build:latest-64bit Docker builds are the actual build path.

nodes.name: Makefile
nodes.summary: RISC OS CModule Makefile for BTSdioTypeA: lists the CMHG header object first (o.BTSdioTypeAHdr) followed by the driver object (o.BTSdioTypeA), sets the include path to h/, and includes the shared CModule rules for AArch64 cross-compilation with BUILD64=1.

nodes.name: README-PHOENIX.md
nodes.summary: Comprehensive Phoenix-port documentation for BTSdioTypeA: covers what changed from the Dec-2024 source, build instructions (local Docker only, not remote), deployment steps, hardware status (SDIO-BT transport is a dead end on CM4 — BT is wired to PL011 UART, not SDIO func3), and the planned pivot to BT-over-UART.

nodes.name: sdio.h
nodes.summary: Public interface header for the SlowArasan SDIO host driver. Declares the sdio_card_t state struct and all exported bus-access functions used by the WiFi and Bluetooth layers above.

nodes.name: sdiodriver.c
nodes.summary: Phoenix SDIODriver SWI provider (chunk 0x59000) that bridges the raw SDIO bus to RISC OS-style client modules such as BTSdioTypeA. Implements RegisterDriver, DeregisterDriver, EnableFunction, ReadBytes, WriteBytes, ClaimIRQ, and ReleaseIRQ SWIs using a polled model.

nodes.name: sdiodriver.h
nodes.summary: Shared ABI header for the Phoenix SDIODriver SWI interface. Defines SWI chunk numbers, sdio_device_id/sdio_func/sdio_driver structs, and sdio_irq_handler — compiled into both the kernel provider and client modules like BTSdioTypeA to ensure binary compatibility.
nodes.languageNotes: The PHOENIX_KERNEL guard splits kernel-internal entry points (sdiodriver_register, sdiodriver_probe_all, sdiodriver_poll, sdiodriver_swi) from the module-facing ABI, so the same header builds cleanly in both contexts.

nodes.name: sdiodriver_swi
nodes.summary: SWI dispatch handler for the SDIODriver chunk (0x59000). Routes offsets 0-6 to RegisterDriver, DeregisterDriver, EnableFunction, ReadBytes, WriteBytes, ClaimIRQ, and ReleaseIRQ implementations.

nodes.name: sdiodriver_probe_all
nodes.summary: Deferred probe runner called from kernel.c after WiFi initialisation. Scans SDIO functions for Bluetooth Type-A interface code (0x2) matching the registered driver's id_table, then calls the driver's probe callback.

nodes.name: sdiodriver_poll
nodes.summary: Polled IRQ service called from the WIMP task loop; invokes the registered client's IRQ handler if the function is enabled, driving BT receive speculatively.

nodes.name: sdiodriver_register
nodes.summary: Registers the SDIODriver SWI provider as a native kernel module at SWI chunk 0x59000 via module_register_native, making its SWIs callable by any RISC OS module.

nodes.name: arp.c
nodes.summary: Implements ARP for Phoenix OS: a 16-entry LRU cache mapping IPs to MACs, ARP request/reply handling, and a blocking resolver that polls GENET RX until a reply arrives. Supports multiple network interfaces so each NIC replies with its own IP and MAC.
nodes.languageNotes: Gratuitous ARP probes from DHCP populate the gateway MAC entry on boot, removing the need for a separate lookup before the first outbound TCP connection.

nodes.name: arp.h
nodes.summary: ARP protocol constants (ARP_OP_REQUEST/REPLY, hardware/protocol types), the arp_hdr_t wire-format struct, and forward declarations of the public ARP API.

nodes.name: dhcp.h
nodes.summary: Public API declarations for the PhoenixDHCP module: state constants, the per-interface dhcp_set_target/dhcp_set_send overrides, DISCOVER/REQUEST/ACK lifecycle calls, and full lease query accessors (get_ip, get_gateway, get_dns, etc.).

nodes.name: ipv4.c
nodes.summary: IPv4 input dispatcher that demultiplexes incoming frames by protocol number to ICMP, TCP, or UDP handlers, plus an ICMP echo-reply generator and an IPv4 output function that builds Ethernet+IP headers and transmits via GENET.

nodes.name: net.h
nodes.summary: Master network header defining the netif_t interface struct (name, MAC, IP, netmask, gateway, send function pointer, up flag), the two global interface instances g_netif_genet and g_netif_wifi, and the public API surface for ARP, IPv4, TCP, and UDP modules.
nodes.languageNotes: The netif_t abstraction (boot651) was the key redesign enabling simultaneous WiFi + GENET operation: each NIC carries its own send() function pointer so ARP replies and ICMP echoes egress on the correct interface.

nodes.name: tcpip.c
nodes.summary: EtherType frame dispatcher that routes incoming Ethernet frames to ARP, IPv4, or IPv6 handlers based on the EtherType field, and initialises the entire Phoenix TCP/IP stack in tcpip_init().

nodes.name: genet_module.c
nodes.summary: Wraps the BCM GENET hardware driver as a RISC OS DCI4 network module, implementing all nine DCI4 SWI offsets, a filter registration list for future DCIShim integration, TX/RX statistics, and service broadcasts for DCIDRIVER_STARTING and DYING events.
nodes.languageNotes: The DCI4 filter list infrastructure is fully wired but handler dispatch is bypassed for now (no MbufManager); genet_module_rx() falls through to net_rx_frame() directly to keep the native TCP/IP stack functional until DCIShim is ready.

nodes.name: table_update
nodes.summary: Caches or refreshes an IP-to-MAC mapping in the 16-entry LRU ARP table, ignoring RFC 5227 probe frames (sender IP 0.0.0.0) and using round-robin eviction for new entries.

nodes.name: arp_resolve
nodes.summary: Looks up a cached MAC address for a given IPv4 address; returns 1 and fills mac_out on hit, 0 on miss.

nodes.name: arp_send_request
nodes.summary: Builds and transmits a 60-byte ARP who-has request frame via genet_send(), using the GENET MAC as the source and broadcasting to resolve an uncached IP.

nodes.name: arp_resolve_blocking
nodes.summary: Blocking ARP MAC resolution: returns immediately on cache hit, otherwise sends an ARP request and polls GENET RX via the ARM Generic Timer until a reply updates the cache or the timeout expires.

nodes.name: send_reply
nodes.summary: Builds and sends an ARP reply frame on the interface that received the request, filling sender hardware/protocol addresses from the netif_t so each NIC replies with its own MAC and IP.

nodes.name: arp_input
nodes.summary: Processes an incoming ARP frame: unconditionally caches the sender's IP-to-MAC mapping, and sends an ARP reply via the arriving interface if the frame is a who-has request targeting that interface's IP.

nodes.name: icmp_input
nodes.summary: Handles ICMP echo requests (type 8) addressed to the receiving interface's IP: swaps Ethernet src/dst and IP src/dst, sets TTL=64, recomputes both the IP header and ICMP checksums, and replies via the arriving netif's send function.

nodes.name: ipv4_input
nodes.summary: Validates the IPv4 version and IHL, then dispatches to icmp_input, tcp_rx, or udp_rx based on the protocol field; silently drops IGMP, ESP, and other unhandled protocols.

nodes.name: ipv4_output
nodes.summary: Builds a complete Ethernet + IPv4 header around a transport-layer payload, computes the IP checksum, and transmits via genet_send(); used by TCP and UDP for outbound datagrams.

nodes.name: tcpip_init
nodes.summary: Initialises the entire Phoenix TCP/IP stack by calling arp_init, ipv4_init, ipv6_init, tcp_init, and udp_init in sequence.

nodes.name: net_rx_frame
nodes.summary: EtherType dispatcher: reads bytes 12–13 of the Ethernet frame and routes to arp_input, ipv4_input, or ipv6_input; silently drops unknown EtherTypes such as LLDP and 802.1Q.

nodes.name: genet_module_init
nodes.summary: Initialises the GENET DCI4 module: clears the filter pool, populates the Dib with the live hardware MAC and capability flags, broadcasts Service_DCIDriverStatus/DCIDRIVER_STARTING to notify listening modules.

nodes.name: genet_module_rx
nodes.summary: RX dispatch: walks the DCI4 filter list matching on EtherType/frame-level, then always forwards the frame to net_rx_frame() so the native Phoenix TCP/IP stack is fed until a proper Internet module registers above via DCI4Filter.

nodes.name: genet_module_tx
nodes.summary: Builds a flat 14-byte Ethernet header around a payload and transmits via genet_send(), updating TX frame/byte/error counters.

nodes.name: genet_module_swi
nodes.summary: Handles all nine DCI4 SWI offsets (Version, Inquire, GetMTU, SetMTU, Transmit, Filter, Stats, MulticastRequest, EntryPoints), providing the complete DCI4 interface surface for DCIShim or any upper-layer network protocol module.

nodes.name: board_info.h
nodes.summary: Header defining the board_info_t struct and the board_info_init / board_info API for the boot-time board-fact cache.

nodes.name: board_info_t
nodes.summary: Struct caching immutable Raspberry Pi board facts: firmware revision, board model/revision/serial, MAC address, ARM/VC memory split, and fixed reference clock rates for UART and EMMC.

nodes.name: mailbox_property.c
nodes.summary: Unified VideoCore mailbox property interface wrapping mbox_call() for all VC firmware operations including board info, power, clocks, USB, and GPIO.

nodes.name: mailbox_property.h
nodes.summary: Header defining all VideoCore mailbox property tag IDs, constants, and public API declarations for mailbox_property.c.

nodes.name: miniuart.c
nodes.summary: BCM2711 mini-UART (AUX/UART1) self-test driver that briefly routes GPIO14/15 to the mini-UART to prove 115200-baud console readability before permanently switching the console away from PL011.

nodes.name: mbox_simple
nodes.summary: Static helper that builds a single-tag mailbox property buffer, calls mbox_call(), and copies response values back to the caller.

nodes.name: mbox_get_firmware_revision
nodes.summary: Returns the VideoCore firmware revision via mailbox tag 0x00000001.

nodes.name: mbox_get_board_model
nodes.summary: Returns the board model number from the VideoCore OTP via mailbox.

nodes.name: mbox_get_board_revision
nodes.summary: Returns the board revision code from the VideoCore OTP via mailbox.

nodes.name: mbox_get_board_serial
nodes.summary: Returns the 64-bit board serial number from the VideoCore OTP via mailbox.

nodes.name: mbox_get_mac_address
nodes.summary: Retrieves the board EUI-48 MAC address from the VideoCore OTP, unpacking two 32-bit words into a 6-byte array.

nodes.name: mbox_get_arm_memory
nodes.summary: Returns the ARM-accessible memory base and size from the VideoCore via mailbox.

nodes.name: mbox_get_vc_memory
nodes.summary: Returns the VideoCore-reserved memory base and size via mailbox.

nodes.name: mbox_get_power_state
nodes.summary: Queries the power state (on/off) of a VC-managed device by device ID.

nodes.name: mbox_set_power_state
nodes.summary: Powers a VC-managed device on or off, optionally blocking until the state takes effect.

nodes.name: mbox_get_clock_rate
nodes.summary: Returns the current rate in Hz for a given VC clock ID via mailbox.

nodes.name: mbox_get_max_clock_rate
nodes.summary: Returns the maximum achievable rate in Hz for a given VC clock ID via mailbox.

nodes.name: mbox_set_clock_rate
nodes.summary: Sets a VC clock to a specific rate in Hz via mailbox.

nodes.name: mbox_power_on_usb
nodes.summary: Powers on the USB host controller device (device ID 3) via mailbox, blocking until the VC confirms.

nodes.name: mbox_notify_xhci_reset
nodes.summary: Asks the VideoCore to load VL805 USB firmware via PCIe using tag 0x00030058; required on Pi 4 boards without SPI EEPROM.

nodes.name: mbox_set_led_state
nodes.summary: Sets the state of a firmware-controlled LED/GPIO pin via mailbox tag 0x00038041.

nodes.name: mbox_set_gpio_state
nodes.summary: Drives a firmware/expander GPIO pin (including CM4 expander pins BT_ON, WL_ON at 128+) via mailbox tag 0x00038041.

nodes.name: mbox_get_gpio_state
nodes.summary: Reads back a firmware/expander GPIO level via mailbox tag 0x00030041; returns 0/1 or -1 on firmware rejection.

nodes.name: mbox_set_gpio_config
nodes.summary: Configures a firmware/expander GPIO pin direction and initial state via mailbox tag 0x00038043.

nodes.name: miniuart_console_selftest
nodes.summary: One-shot proof-of-concept: briefly routes GPIO14/15 to the mini-UART, prints a readability banner at 115200 baud, then returns the pins to PL011 — proving the permanent console switch is safe.

nodes.name: mu_init
nodes.summary: Initializes the mini-UART hardware at a given baud rate by querying the live core clock via mbox_get_clock_rate() and computing the divisor.

nodes.name: gpio_func
nodes.summary: Sets the alternate function of a GPIO pin by writing to the GPFSEL register.

nodes.name: mu_putc
nodes.summary: Writes a single character to the mini-UART TX FIFO, spinning until space is available.

nodes.name: mu_puts
nodes.summary: Writes a null-terminated string to the mini-UART, inserting CR before each LF.

nodes.name: DESIGN_provider_abstraction.md
nodes.summary: Defines the Phoenix provider/client driver abstraction pattern — kernel SWI providers own board-specific hardware, loadable client modules use them through a stable interface — with a decision checklist and table of current/planned providers.

nodes.name: BoardInfo
nodes.summary: RISC OS CModule C source implementing the *BoardInfo command, which decodes the Raspberry Pi board revision code (bit-field extraction for model, SoC, RAM) by calling the kernel BoardInfo SWI provider and printing human-readable results.
nodes.languageNotes: Extension-less RISC OS convention: c/BoardInfo is the C source. Uses _kernel_oswrch for character output and _kernel_swi for SWI calls via Norcroft/CMunge ABI.

nodes.name: BoardInfo
nodes.summary: C header defining the board_info_buf_t structure (52-byte naturally-aligned layout matching the kernel's board_info.c) and the inline boardinfo_getinfo() helper that issues SWI BoardInfo_GetInfo (0x5C000).
nodes.languageNotes: Buffer layout must match the kernel provider byte-for-byte; u64 first, then u32s, then bytes to avoid padding differences between Norcroft and gcc on AArch64.

nodes.name: BoardInfoHdr
nodes.summary: CMunge 64-bit module descriptor defining the BoardInfo RISC OS module title, help string, initialisation/finalisation entry points, and the *BoardInfo command keyword table.
nodes.languageNotes: CMunge -64bit format; comments are run through the C preprocessor, so apostrophes must be avoided. cmd_no 0 maps to the BoardInfo command handler.

nodes.name: Makefile
nodes.summary: RISC OS AMU Makefile building the BoardInfo CModule: compiles the CMunge-generated header object first, then the C source, and links via the shared CModule include rule; supports BUILD64=1 for AArch64/Phoenix.

nodes.name: README-PHOENIX.md
nodes.summary: Developer documentation covering the *BoardInfo command output, the BoardInfo SWI ABI (chunk 0x5C000), Docker-based local build instructions, deployment to the Pi SD card, and the new-style Pi revision code bit-field decode reference.

nodes.name: VersionNum
nodes.summary: Version number header for the BoardInfo module, defining Module_MajorVersion (0.01), date (21 Jun 2026), component name, and related version macros consumed by the build system.

nodes.name: model_name
nodes.summary: Maps a Pi revision-code type field (bits 4-11) to a human-readable model name string covering all known Pi variants from Model A through Compute Module 5 Lite.

nodes.name: soc_name
nodes.summary: Maps the processor field (bits 12-15) of the Pi revision code to a SoC name string (BCM2835 through BCM2712).

nodes.name: mem_name
nodes.summary: Maps the memory field (bits 20-22) of the Pi revision code to a human-readable RAM size string (256 MB through 16 GB).

nodes.name: do_info
nodes.summary: Core implementation of *BoardInfo: calls boardinfo_getinfo() via SWI, decodes new-style revision codes using bit-field extraction, and prints model/SoC/RAM/memory map/serial/MAC/clocks to the RISC OS text output stream.

nodes.name: BoardInfo_Init
nodes.summary: RISC OS module initialisation entry point called by the kernel when the module is loaded; prints a startup banner and returns no error.

nodes.name: BoardInfo_Final
nodes.summary: RISC OS module finalisation entry point; performs no cleanup and always returns success.

nodes.name: BoardInfo_Command
nodes.summary: RISC OS *command dispatch entry point; routes cmd_no 0 (*BoardInfo) to do_info() to print board identity information.

nodes.name: boardinfo_getinfo
nodes.summary: Inline helper that issues SWI BoardInfo_GetInfo (0x5C000) with a pointer to the caller's board_info_buf_t, filling it with kernel-cached board facts; casts via intptr_t to avoid 64-bit address truncation.

nodes.name: HALInfo
nodes.summary: Main C source for the HALInfo RISC OS module; implements the *HALInfo command that queries the kernel HALInfo SWI provider (chunk 0x5D000) and prints DT-discovered hardware layout including RAM, GIC addresses, peripheral base, CPU count, and PCIe slot occupant with VID:DID decoding.
nodes.languageNotes: RISC OS file-naming convention: the file lives in the c/ directory with no extension; output is written character-by-character via _kernel_oswrch rather than stdio.

nodes.name: pcie_name
nodes.summary: Maps a PCIe VID:DID pair to a human-readable device name; distinguishes the Pi 4 VIA VL805 xHCI controller from Micron and Crucial/Micron NVMe SSDs found in CM4 slots.

nodes.name: do_info
nodes.summary: Core display routine for *HALInfo: calls halinfo_getinfo() to fill a hal_info_buf_t, then prints each DT-discovered field (DT validity, Pi model, CPU count, RAM, peripheral/UART/GIC bases, CPU0 release address, and PCIe occupant with VID:DID lookup).

nodes.name: HALInfo_Init
nodes.summary: RISC OS module initialisation entry point called by the kernel when the module is loaded; prints a version banner and returns no error.

nodes.name: HALInfo_Final
nodes.summary: RISC OS module finalisation entry point; performs no cleanup and always returns success.

nodes.name: HALInfo_Command
nodes.summary: RISC OS *command dispatcher generated by CMunge; dispatches cmd_no==0 to do_info() to implement the *HALInfo command.

nodes.name: HALInfo
nodes.summary: C header defining the HALInfo SWI ABI (chunk 0x5D000): declares hal_info_buf_t with naturally aligned u64/u32/u8 fields matching kernel/devicetree.c, and provides the inline halinfo_getinfo() helper that calls HALInfo_GetInfo via _kernel_swi.
nodes.languageNotes: Field order is fixed (u64s first, then u32s, then bytes) to guarantee zero-padding alignment in both Norcroft (RISC OS compiler) and gcc; reordering would break the ABI with the kernel provider.

nodes.name: HALInfoHdr
nodes.summary: CMunge 64-bit module descriptor for HALInfo; wires the RISC OS module header (title, help string, init/final entry points, and the *HALInfo command keyword table) to the C functions in c/HALInfo.
nodes.languageNotes: CMunge processes this through the C preprocessor, so standard C comment punctuation (apostrophes) is avoided; the -64bit flag selects AArch64 module format without a runnable start address.

nodes.name: Makefile
nodes.summary: RISC OS CModule build recipe for HALInfo; links the CMunge-generated header object (o.HALInfoHdr) with the C object (o.HALInfo) via the shared CModule include, and declares explicit header dependencies for reproducible AArch64 builds.
nodes.languageNotes: Targets use RISC OS o. object prefix convention; the CModule include provides the shared link rules; BUILD64=1 selects the 64-bit AArch64 toolchain (riscos64-amu).

nodes.name: README-PHOENIX.md

nodes.name: BTUart
nodes.summary: Full Bluetooth host stack implementation as a loadable RISC OS module, providing HCI inquiry, SSP pairing, L2CAP channel management, SDP service discovery, and HID keyboard input over the thin BTHW SWI hardware abstraction layer.

nodes.name: do_scan
nodes.summary: Runs an HCI inquiry for ~12 seconds, deduplicates found device addresses, requests the remote friendly name for each, and populates the g_scan device list for subsequent pairing or L2CAP commands.

nodes.name: do_pair
nodes.summary: Drives the full SSP pairing state machine (Create Connection + HCI event dispatch for PIN, user-confirmation, passkey, and link-key events), stores the resulting bond key via hw_savekey, and auto-continues into do_hid() on success.

nodes.name: acl_open
nodes.summary: Opens an ACL link to a given Bluetooth address, optionally supplying the stored link key to authenticate; returns the HCI connection handle on success or 0 on failure.

nodes.name: l2cap_open
nodes.summary: Opens an L2CAP channel to the given PSM, handling both outgoing Connection Request and incoming Connection Request (device-initiated), correctly treating result=0x0001 as PENDING (not failure), completing configuration exchange, and returning the remote DCID on success.
nodes.languageNotes: Boot685 fix: the old `if (result) break` bail was replaced with a three-way branch on 0x0000 (success), 0x0001 (pending, keep looping), and >=0x02 (refused, break). Monotonic g_sig_id ensures unique signalling IDs per outstanding L2CAP request.

nodes.name: sdp_search
nodes.summary: Sends an SDP ServiceSearch request and iterates each returned record handle, querying ServiceClassIDList via sdp_class() and printing human-readable service names.

nodes.name: do_l2cap
nodes.summary: Implements the *BTL2CAP command: opens an ACL link then an L2CAP SDP channel to the selected scanned device and triggers full SDP service enumeration.

nodes.name: do_hid
nodes.summary: Implements the *BTHID command: authenticates the ACL link, enables link encryption, opens HID control (PSM 0x0011) and interrupt (PSM 0x0013) L2CAP channels, then hands live HID polling to the kernel via BTHW_HidLive so keyboard reports inject directly into RISC OS.

nodes.name: do_discs
nodes.summary: Enumerates all registered FileCore discs by calling discinfo_count() and discinfo_get(), then prints a formatted table with index, name, media type, block size, and total size for each disc; marks the boot disc.

nodes.name: media_name

nodes.name: prsize

nodes.name: prpad

nodes.name: DiscInfo

nodes.name: discinfo_count

nodes.name: do_ifconfig
nodes.summary: Core logic for *Ifconfig: calls ifconfig_count(), iterates interfaces with ifconfig_get(), and formats name, status, IP, MAC, netmask, and gateway to OS output for each.

nodes.name: Ifconfig_Init

nodes.name: Ifconfig

nodes.name: ifconfig_count

nodes.name: filecore.c
nodes.summary: Phoenix FileCore/ADFS filesystem driver: handles disc discovery (MBR/GPT/boot-block), multi-zone sector-map traversal, SBPr NewDir directory parsing, a multi-disc block-device registry, a DiscInfo SWI provider (chunk 0x5E000) that reports physical hardware geometry, and the write path (find_path/resolve_parent/dr_create_file/dr_save_object) used by bt_uart.c for BTKeys persistence.
nodes.languageNotes: Bare-metal C for AArch64/RISC OS environment; no libc — uses custom uart_puts diagnostics and kmalloc/kfree. The ADFS new-map zone reader uses bit-addressed allocation maps (adfs_read_bits) with a non-trivial bit-position-to-LBA conversion (fc_bit_addr_to_data_lba). Critical design note: discinfo_swi intentionally reads bd->size/bd->block_size/bd->name (set from EXT_CSD/NVMe IDENTIFY at hardware probe time) rather than the on-disc DiscRecord to avoid stale geometry on cloned media.

nodes.name: filecore_init
nodes.summary: Boot-time disc initialisation: reads MBR/GPT, probes boot-block and zone-0 DiscRecords from each registered block device, extracts ADFS zone parameters, and populates the global disc-geometry state used by all later filesystem operations.

nodes.name: filecore_list_root
nodes.summary: Full ADFS new-map zone scan: iterates all map zones, reads each zone's DiscRecord and bit-allocation map, converts fragment IDs to LBAs, reads and dumps root directory entries in SBPr NewDir format with verbose UART diagnostics.

nodes.name: filecore_get_child_entry
nodes.summary: Resolves a directory SIN to its LBA, reads the directory sector, parses SBPr NewDir 28-byte entries, and returns the nth entry (name, SIN, size, load/exec, isdir) to callers performing path traversal.

nodes.name: fc_ida_to_data_lba
nodes.summary: Converts an ADFS internal disc address (IDA/SIN) to a physical LBA by scanning the new-map zone headers and bit-allocation map for the correct zone and fragment offset.

nodes.name: adfs_chain_traverse
nodes.summary: Traverses an ADFS fragment chain from a starting fragment ID and byte offset, resolving each link through the new-map zone bit-allocation structures to read contiguous file data across zone boundaries.

nodes.name: filecore_step6_load_module
nodes.summary: Boot step 6: locates and loads RISC OS modules from the $.Modules and $.Kernel directories on the ADFS disc, reading them via the zone-map chain traversal and handing them to the module loader.

nodes.name: filecore_find_path
nodes.summary: Resolves a filesystem path string (e.g. '$.BTKeys') to a directory entry by iterating path components through filecore_get_child_entry; used by the BTKeys write path in bt_uart.c.

nodes.name: filecore_resolve_parent
nodes.summary: Resolves all but the final component of a filesystem path to obtain the parent directory SIN and the leaf filename; called before create/save operations to determine where to write a new object.

nodes.name: filecore_save_open
nodes.summary: Opens or creates a file on the ADFS volume for writing, returning the SIN, allocated capacity, parent SIN, and load/exec stamps; the write counterpart to filecore_find_path.

nodes.name: discinfo_swi
nodes.summary: SWI handler for the DiscInfo chunk (0x5E000): fills a disc_info_t struct from the physical block-device registry using hardware-probed geometry (size, block_size, name) rather than the potentially stale on-disc DiscRecord, ensuring correct results on cloned media.

nodes.name: discinfo_register
nodes.summary: Registers the DiscInfo SWI handler with the kernel's SWI dispatch table for chunk 0x5E000 so that user-mode and module code can query physical disc geometry.

nodes.name: fc_try_load_modules_from_dir
nodes.summary: Scans a named ADFS directory for module files and loads each one into the kernel module table, used during boot to populate modules from $.Modules.

nodes.name: fc_scan_gpt
nodes.summary: Scans a GPT partition table on a block device, identifies ADFS partitions by GUID type, and returns the LBA and sector count of the first matching ADFS partition.

nodes.name: fc_bit_addr_to_data_lba
nodes.summary: Converts a raw bit address within an ADFS new-map zone buffer to the corresponding disc LBA, accounting for zone-spare bits, used-bits offset, and sectors-per-logical-fragment-allocation-unit.

nodes.name: filecore_populate_root_cache
nodes.summary: Parses a SBPr NewDir directory buffer and inserts each entry into the in-memory root directory cache used to answer filecore_get_root_entry queries without repeated disc reads.

nodes.name: filecore_populate_root_cache_dr
nodes.summary: Top-level entry point that reads the root directory from disc and delegates to filecore_populate_root_cache to fill the cached entry array.

nodes.name: filecore_root_cache_add
nodes.summary: Appends a single directory entry (name, SIN, size, isdir, load, exec) to the in-memory root directory cache, growing the cache array as needed.

nodes.name: filecore_dr_find_path
nodes.summary: Path resolution variant that uses an alternate disc reader path (dr_*) to find a file or directory by path string, returning its SIN, size, and isdir flag.

nodes.name: filecore_dr_resolve_parent
nodes.summary: Alternate-reader variant of filecore_resolve_parent: walks all but the final path component via dr_* reads, returning parent SIN, existing-object SIN/capacity, and the leaf filename.

nodes.name: obey_exec_line
nodes.summary: Executes a single line from an ADFS !Boot/!Run Obey script, handling keyword dispatch (Set, Echo, RMLoad, Desktop, etc.) and driving the early-boot scripting layer.

nodes.name: filecore_exec_obey
nodes.summary: Parses and executes a multi-line Obey script buffer line by line by delegating each line to obey_exec_line.

nodes.name: filecore_parse_mbr
nodes.summary: Parses a 512-byte MBR sector, identifies ADFS/FileCore partition entries, and returns the partition type, LBA start, and sector count for the first matching entry.

nodes.name: adfs_hugo_brute_scan
nodes.summary: Brute-force sector scan that searches a range of LBAs for Hugo-format (old ADFS) directory signatures, used as a fallback when the new-map zone traversal cannot locate a directory.

nodes.name: filecore_sd_write_test
nodes.summary: Write-path integration test: writes a known pattern to an ADFS file on the SD card and verifies the data can be read back, exercising the full dr_create_file/dr_write path.

nodes.name: filecore_sd_save_test
nodes.summary: Save-path integration test: creates and writes a multi-sector file via dr_save_object and confirms correct byte counts and attributes after save.

nodes.name: filecore_bootdisc_write_test
nodes.summary: Write-path test targeting the boot disc specifically, covering cross-device write scenarios where the boot disc is a different block device than the bound disc.

nodes.name: filecore_cat_print
nodes.summary: Implements a bare-metal 'cat' command: resolves a path, reads the file contents sector by sector, and prints the data to the UART console.

nodes.name: filecore_resolve_path
nodes.summary: Strips the disc/filesystem prefix from a full Phoenix path string (e.g. 'ADFS::HardDisc4.$.foo') and returns the canonical path root and remaining component, normalising path syntax before traversal.

nodes.name: adfs_dump_hugo_dir
nodes.summary: Dumps the raw contents of an ADFS Hugo (old-map) format directory buffer to the UART, used for diagnostic inspection during boot-time directory reads.

nodes.name: adfs_read_bits
nodes.summary: Reads an arbitrary-width (up to 32-bit) field from a byte buffer at a given bit position, the fundamental primitive used by the ADFS new-map zone reader to extract fragment IDs and zone data.

nodes.name: filecore_show_results
nodes.summary: Prints a summary of the disc scan results — registered block devices, zone counts, disc names, and detected partition geometry — to the UART console.

nodes.name: filecore_multidisc_test
nodes.summary: Integration test for multi-disc registry: registers multiple block devices, binds them by index/name, and verifies that disc lookup functions return correct entries for each registered device.

nodes.name: dhcp.c
nodes.summary: Phoenix OS DHCP client and Ifconfig SWI provider. Implements the full DHCP state machine (DISCOVER → OFFER → REQUEST → ACK/NACK → BOUND with retransmit and gratuitous ARP), plus the ifconfig_swi/ifconfig_register functions that expose wired (genet) and WiFi interface status to userspace via SWI chunk 0x5F000.
nodes.languageNotes: The ifcfg_buf_t struct must be byte-identical between kernel (GCC) and the Norcroft-compiled Ifconfig RISC OS module — a cross-ABI constraint documented in the boot687 history. A race condition in boot345 required setting DHCP state BEFORE calling genet_send; retransmit logic resets last_net immediately after dhcp_start.

nodes.name: dhcp_rx
nodes.summary: Processes incoming DHCP frames. Validates the packet (XID, message type), handles OFFER (→ REQUEST), ACK (→ BOUND, extracts IP/gateway/netmask/DNS/lease), and NACK (→ restart). Sends gratuitous ARP on successful BOUND transition.

nodes.name: dhcp_module_init
nodes.summary: Module-level initialiser that waits for genet link up, then runs the DHCP polling loop until a lease is obtained. Called by the kernel module system at boot to bring up the wired network interface with an IP address.

nodes.name: ifconfig_swi
nodes.summary: SWI handler for the Ifconfig provider (chunk 0x5F000). Fills an ifcfg_buf_t for either the wired genet interface or the WiFi interface based on the requested index, exposing interface name, up/down state, IP address, MAC, netmask, and gateway to callers.

nodes.name: ifconfig_register
nodes.summary: Registers the Ifconfig native SWI provider (chunk 0x5F000) with the kernel's SWI dispatch table via module_register_native, making ifconfig_swi callable from userspace modules.

nodes.name: dhcp_init
nodes.summary: Initialises the DHCP client state with the provided MAC address, configures the send callback target, and resets all lease fields to zero.

nodes.name: dhcp_tick
nodes.summary: Periodic timer callback that drives DHCP retransmission. On BOUND transitions sends a gratuitous ARP; on timeout retransmits the last DHCP message to handle packet loss.

nodes.name: rp1_gem.c
nodes.summary: Pi 5 Cadence GEM Ethernet MAC driver implementing staged bring-up: Stage 1 probes the Module ID via MMIO, Stage 2 releases the BCM54213 PHY from RP1 GPIO reset and negotiates MDIO link, Stage 3 initialises 64-bit DMA descriptor rings with the +64 GB PCIe address offset, and Stage 4 exposes polled TX/RX. Pi 5 counterpart to drivers/net/genet.c.

nodes.name: rp1_gem.h
nodes.summary: Public header for the RP1 Cadence GEM Ethernet driver, declaring the staged bring-up entry point (rp1_gem_probe), TX/RX polled I/O functions, and key frame-size constants for Pi 5.

nodes.name: sdhci_brcmstb.c
nodes.summary: Pi 5 WiFi SDIO host driver for the BCM2712 SDHCI-brcmstb controller (MMIO 0x1001100000), covering pinctrl mux setup for CYW43455 SDIO pads, WL_ON GPIO assertion, vendor CFG-block initialisation, and a Stage 0 read-only probe. Pi 5 counterpart to drivers/sdio/sdio.c.

nodes.name: rp1_gem_probe
nodes.summary: Stage 1 entry point: ioremaps the GEM MMIO window, reads the Module ID register, and on success chains into rp1_gem_phy_init (Stage 2) and rp1_gem_rings_init (Stage 3). Returns -1 if the controller is not yet reachable.

nodes.name: rp1_gem_phy_reset
nodes.summary: Releases the BCM54213 PHY from hardware reset by configuring RP1 GPIO 32 (bank 1, local index 4) as a software-driven output via the RIO register block, toggling it active-low for 5 ms then high for 20 ms before MDIO access.

nodes.name: rp1_gem_phy_init
nodes.summary: Stage 2 PHY bring-up: releases the PHY reset, enables MDIO management port with a safe clock divisor, scans all 32 MDIO addresses for the BCM54213, issues a software reset and autonegotiation restart, and polls up to 3 s for link-up.

nodes.name: rp1_gem_rings_init
nodes.summary: Stage 3 MAC bring-up: initialises 64-bit DMA descriptor rings applying the +64 GB RP1 PCIe address offset to every ring and buffer pointer, programs the MAC address from VideoCore OTP, configures NCFGR speed/duplex from PHY autoneg, and enables RX/TX with a diagnostic poll after 1.5 s to verify frames are DMA-ing into the ring.

nodes.name: rp1_gem_send
nodes.summary: Transmits one raw Ethernet frame by writing it into the TX DMA buffer (with PCIe address offset), programming the GEM TX descriptor with LAST/WRAP flags, kicking the transmitter via NCR.TSTART, and polling for the MAC's USED acknowledgement.

nodes.name: rp1_gem_poll_rx
nodes.summary: Polls the current RX descriptor for a received frame: copies the frame out of the DMA buffer, returns ownership of the descriptor to the MAC by clearing the USED bit, and advances the ring index.

nodes.name: pi5_sdhci_probe
nodes.summary: Stage 0 read-only probe: ioremaps the BCM2712 WiFi SDHCI host, reads the HOST_VERSION, CAPABILITIES, and PRESENT_STATE registers, and rejects all-ones responses that indicate the controller is not yet clocked or decoded.

nodes.name: pi5_pinctrl_wifi
nodes.summary: Configures BCM2712 pinctrl function-select and pull values for the CYW43455 SDIO interface: sets gpio28 WL_ON to gpio function, gpio30-35 CLK/CMD/DAT0-3 to sd2 function, and applies pull-up on CMD and DAT lines for clean CRC framing.

nodes.name: pi5_sdhci_cfginit
nodes.summary: Writes the BCM2712 SDHCI vendor CFG block (at host+0x400): sets SD_PIN_SEL to SD mode (not eMMC) to fix end-bit errors, and asserts card-presence override for the non-removable CYW43455 WiFi chip.

nodes.name: pi5_wlon_assert
nodes.summary: Powers on the CYW43455 WiFi chip by asserting BCM2712 GIO GPIO 28 (WL_ON, active-high) and waiting 150 ms for the chip's power-up sequence to complete before SDIO enumeration.

nodes.name: mmu.c
nodes.summary: AArch64 MMU initialisation for Phoenix OS: builds a flat identity-map page-table hierarchy (L1 1 GB blocks, L2 2 MB splits, L3 4 KB pages) covering Pi 4 and Pi 5 memory layouts including the Pi 5 NVMe PCIe window (l1_table[110] = 0x1B80000000, Device-mapped).
nodes.languageNotes: Inline assembly enables MMU/D-cache/I-cache in a single SCTLR_EL1 RMW after loading TTBR0/TTBR1. TLB invalidation uses TLBI VMALLE1IS (inner-shareable broadcast) for multi-core safety.

nodes.name: mmu_init
nodes.summary: Builds the AArch64 identity page-table hierarchy (L1/L2/L3), marks the .xhci_dma section Normal Non-Cacheable, GPU RAM Non-Cacheable, Pi 4/5 peripheral and PCIe windows Device-nGnRnE (including the Pi 5 NVMe window at l1_table[110] = 0x1B80000000), then programs MAIR/TCR/TTBR and enables MMU+caches in SCTLR_EL1.

nodes.name: mmu_tlb_invalidate_all
nodes.summary: Issues TLBI VMALLE1IS + DSB ISH + ISB to flush all TLB entries broadcast to all inner-shareable PEs.

nodes.name: mmu_tlb_invalidate_addr
nodes.summary: Invalidates the TLB entry for a single virtual address using TLBI VAE1IS.

nodes.name: boot.S
nodes.summary: AArch64 reset-vector stub — parks secondary CPUs, configures EL2 timer access registers for Pi5 compatibility, drops from EL2 to EL1 via eret, sets the kernel stack, installs VBAR_EL1 exception vectors, zeroes BSS, and calls kernel_main.
nodes.languageNotes: Includes Pi5-specific cnthctl_el2/cntvoff_el2 setup: BL31 on Pi5 leaves timer registers trapping, so orr #3 into cnthctl_el2 is required before any CNTP_* access in EL1.

nodes.name: devicetree.c
nodes.summary: FDT/DTB parser that extracts RAM layout, CPU count and release addresses, /soc address-translation ranges, and GIC base addresses (arm,gic-400 for Pi4, arm,gic-v3 for Pi5), and registers the HALInfo SWI provider exposing DT-discovered hardware facts to loadable modules.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses volatile byte-by-byte reads throughout to defeat -O2 load-merging that caused pre-MMU alignment faults on BCM2711 (bug392/fix393).

nodes.name: device_tree_parse
nodes.summary: Main DTB parse entry — validates FDT magic, identifies board type from root compatible string, then delegates to parse_memory, parse_cpus, parse_soc_ranges, and parse_gic, setting dt_valid on success.

nodes.name: detect_nr_cpus
nodes.summary: Returns the CPU count discovered from /cpus DT nodes, falling back to 4 if DT was not parsed successfully.

nodes.name: halinfo_swi
nodes.summary: SWI handler for HALInfo chunk 0x5D000 — populates a hal_info_buf_t with DT-discovered memory layout, GIC bases, peripheral base, UART base, CPU release address, PCIe device ID, CPU count, and board model for use by loadable modules.

nodes.name: halinfo_register
nodes.summary: Registers the HALInfo native module providing the HALInfo SWI chunk (0x5D000) for loadable module queries about DT-discovered hardware layout.

nodes.name: periph_base.c
nodes.summary: Board-aware peripheral MMIO base detection — probes BCM2711 and BCM2712 System Timer CLO registers for liveness (requiring counter advancement, not just a non-zero read), sets peripheral_base and pi_model globals, and provides accessor functions for GPIO, UART, and Mailbox bases with Pi5 mailbox offset correction.

nodes.name: detect_peripheral_base
nodes.summary: Probes System Timer CLO at Pi4-low (0xFE003004), Pi4-high/CM4 (0x47E003004), and Pi5 (0x107C003004) addresses by requiring the counter to advance between two reads; sets peripheral_base and pi_model accordingly.

nodes.name: wdog_disable
