nodes.summary: Disables the BCM2711 PM watchdog by writing zero to PM_WDOG and clearing the WRCFG field of PM_RSTC with the required 0x5A password, followed by a DSB barrier — called on Pi4/CM4 only before UART init to prevent USB enumeration timeouts from triggering a hardware reboot.

nodes.name: get_mailbox_base
nodes.summary: Returns the VideoCore mailbox MMIO base, selecting offset 0x13880 for Pi5 (BCM2712) or 0xB880 for Pi4/CM4 (BCM2711) relative to peripheral_base.

nodes.name: irq.c
nodes.summary: BCM2711/BCM2712 GIC-400 (GICv2) interrupt controller driver that initialises the distributor and CPU interface, manages the IRQ handler table, and dispatches interrupts from the AArch64 EL1 exception vector. Supports board-aware GIC base address selection at runtime (Pi 4 defaults vs Pi 5 hard-coded addresses) and includes SGI/IPI support for future SMP use.

nodes.name: irq_init
nodes.summary: Initialises the complete interrupt subsystem: clears the handler table, selects the correct GIC base address (Pi 5 hard-coded, Pi 4 from DT or default), then calls gicd_init() and gicc_init() to configure hardware.

nodes.name: irq_dispatch
nodes.summary: Called from the AArch64 EL1 IRQ exception vector; reads GICC_IAR to acknowledge the interrupt, looks up and calls the registered C handler, then writes GICC_EOIR to signal end-of-interrupt.

nodes.name: irq_set_handler
nodes.summary: Registers a C handler function and private data pointer for a given GIC IRQ vector number in the software handler table.

nodes.name: send_ipi
nodes.summary: Sends a Software Generated Interrupt (SGI) to a bitmask of target CPUs by writing GICD_SGIR; used for future SMP inter-processor communication.

nodes.name: framebuffer.c
nodes.summary: Mailbox-based GPU framebuffer driver supporting both 16bpp (Pi 5 RGB565) and 32bpp (Pi 4) depths, with a full software drawing library (pixels, rects, lines, circles, 8x8 font text) and a scrolling text console (con_printf) used for early boot status output. Also provides a 2x-scaled arrow mouse cursor with save-under restore.
nodes.languageNotes: Pi 5 VideoCore returns a 16bpp RGB565 framebuffer even when 32 bpp is requested; depth is derived from the pitch returned by the mailbox rather than the requested depth, and px_to565/px_from565 helpers convert on every pixel write/read.

nodes.name: fb_init
nodes.summary: Initialises the VideoCore framebuffer via a multi-tag mailbox property message, then reads back the GPU address, pitch, and derives the real bit depth. Draws four corner-colour markers to verify pixel writes work.

nodes.name: fb_set_pixel
nodes.summary: Writes a single pixel at (x,y), dispatching to 16bpp RGB565 or 32bpp word write based on fb.bpp.

nodes.name: fb_clear
nodes.summary: Clears the entire framebuffer to a solid colour, handling both 16bpp and 32bpp modes.

nodes.name: fb_draw_char
nodes.summary: Renders a single character from the 8x8 bitmap font with foreground/background colours.

nodes.name: fb_draw_string_scaled
nodes.summary: Renders a string using the 8x8 font at an integer scale factor, used for the title bar and version tag in gpu_init.

nodes.name: con_init
nodes.summary: Initialises the software text console by computing grid dimensions from framebuffer size and clearing the character buffer.

nodes.name: con_putc
nodes.summary: Posts a single character to the on-screen console, handling newline, carriage-return, tab, backspace, and automatic scroll when the last row is reached.

nodes.name: con_printf
nodes.summary: Minimal printf-style formatter (%s, %d, %u, %x, %c) that writes directly to the on-screen framebuffer console, used by bt_print() during BT firmware download when serial may be dropping bytes.

nodes.name: fb_get_pixel
nodes.summary: Reads a pixel from the framebuffer with correct 16bpp/32bpp depth handling; required by the cursor save-under to avoid a coloured pointer trail on Pi 5.

nodes.name: cursor_blit
nodes.summary: Saves the framebuffer area under the cursor, then draws the 2x-scaled 8x10 arrow cursor in two passes: white halo then black fill.

nodes.name: cursor_update
nodes.summary: Moves the hardware-rendered cursor to a new position: clamps to framebuffer bounds, restores the old save-under, then blits the cursor at the new location.

nodes.name: gpu.c
nodes.summary: Board-aware GPU initialisation: tries framebuffer resolutions from 1080p down to 480p, sets mouse bounds on success, then composites the RISC OS-inspired desktop chrome (title bar, divider, grey background, console) and marks the framebuffer ready.

nodes.name: gpu_init
nodes.summary: Iterates over a resolution table (1080p, 720p, 480p) calling fb_init() until one succeeds, then sets up the RISC OS desktop chrome and initialises the on-screen console. Signals progress via LED blink codes.

nodes.name: nvme.c
nodes.summary: NVMe PCIe SSD controller driver for Phoenix OS supporting both BCM2711 (Pi4/CM4) and BCM2712 (Pi5) with board-aware DMA offsets; initialises admin and I/O queues, performs IDENTIFY, and registers the drive as a native-sector block device.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses AArch64 inline assembly (dsb sy, mrs cntpct_el0) for memory barriers and cycle-count polling; g_nvme_dma_offset is selected at runtime via get_pi_model() so a single binary runs on Pi4/CM4 (0xC0000000) and Pi5 (0x10_00000000).

nodes.name: nvme_init_controller
nodes.summary: Full 5-stage NVMe controller bring-up: board-aware DMA offset selection, CAP/VS probe, admin queue setup, controller enable, IDENTIFY (controller + namespace), I/O queue creation, LBA-0 read, and blockdev registration.

nodes.name: nvme_submit
nodes.summary: Submits a single NVMe command to a queue's submission ring, rings the SQ doorbell, then poll-waits on the completion queue using phase-bit tracking; returns 0 on success or -1 on error/timeout.

nodes.name: nvme_create_io_queue
nodes.summary: Creates the I/O completion and submission queue pair (QID 1) via admin CREATE_IO_CQ and CREATE_IO_SQ commands and wires up the doorbell pointers.

nodes.name: nvme_read_native
nodes.summary: Reads an arbitrary count of native-sized NVMe blocks from a given LBA into a caller buffer, chunking transfers to fit within the 4 KB PRP page limit.

nodes.name: nvme_write_native
nodes.summary: Writes an arbitrary count of native-sized blocks at a given LBA from a caller buffer, chunking to the 4 KB PRP limit and copying through the NC DMA bounce buffer.

nodes.name: nvme_wait_ready
nodes.summary: Polls CSTS.RDY until it reaches the desired state (0 or 1) or a 5-second timeout expires, returning -1 if the controller signals a fatal status.

nodes.name: nvme_read_blocks
nodes.summary: Public block-read stub returning ENOSYS; the functional path goes through the blockdev interface registered in nvme_init_controller.

nodes.name: nvme_write_blocks
nodes.summary: Public block-write stub returning ENOSYS; the functional path goes through the blockdev interface registered in nvme_init_controller.

nodes.name: sdio.c
nodes.summary: BCM2711 SlowArasan SDIO host controller driver (EMMC1 at 0x300000) targeting the CYW43455 WiFi+BT combo chip; implements host reset, clock setup, GPIO mux, CMD52/CMD53 primitives, card probe, and bus-width switching.
nodes.languageNotes: Handles a Pi5 (BCM2712 SDHCI-brcmstb) code path inside sdio_host_init; the CMD5 CENDERR end-bit tolerance in sdio_send_cmd is a Pi5-specific quirk for R3/R4 responses. Control1 requires 32-bit RMW only — sub-word writes are explicitly forbidden.

nodes.name: sdio_init
nodes.summary: Top-level SDIO initialisation entry point: calls sdio_host_init then sdio_probe, and dumps the function map on success.

nodes.name: sdio_probe
nodes.summary: SDIO card enumeration: CMD0 idle, CMD5 voltage negotiation, CMD3 RCA assignment, CMD7 card select, clock ramp to 25 MHz, 4-bit bus switch, and CCCR/FBR identity readout.

nodes.name: sdio_host_init
nodes.summary: Initialises the SDIO host controller for either BCM2711 SlowArasan or Pi5 SDHCI-brcmstb: sets base address, configures GPIO or Pi5 pin control, resets controller, sets 400 kHz identification clock, and enables bus power.

nodes.name: sdio_send_cmd
nodes.summary: Issues a single SD/SDIO command, waits for CMD inhibit, optionally DAT inhibit, polls for completion or error, handles Pi5 CENDERR end-bit quirk, and returns the response words.

nodes.name: sdio_cmd52_read
nodes.summary: Reads a single byte from an SDIO function register using CMD52 IO_RW_DIRECT and validates the R5 response flags.

nodes.name: sdio_cmd52_write
nodes.summary: Writes a single byte to an SDIO function register using CMD52 IO_RW_DIRECT and validates the R5 response flags.

nodes.name: sdio_cmd53_write
nodes.summary: Multi-byte SDIO write using CMD53 IO_RW_EXTENDED in block or byte mode (func1=64B blocks, func2=512B blocks), fills the FIFO via PIO, and waits for transfer complete.

nodes.name: sdio_cmd53_read
nodes.summary: Multi-byte SDIO read using CMD53 IO_RW_EXTENDED in byte mode, draining the FIFO via PIO into the caller buffer.

nodes.name: sdio_cmd53_setup
nodes.summary: Prepares a DMA-backed CMD53 block write by issuing the command and waiting for WRITERDY, leaving the FIFO open for an external DMA engine to fill.

nodes.name: sdio_cmd53_finish
nodes.summary: Polls for DATADONE after a DMA-backed CMD53 write completes and resets the data circuit on error.

nodes.name: sdio_set_clock
nodes.summary: Computes the BCM2711 10-bit Arasan clock divider from the EMMC mailbox clock rate to reach the requested frequency and enables the SD clock output.

nodes.name: sdio_dump_functions
nodes.summary: Reads and prints the SDIO standard interface code and block size for each I/O function via FBR, identifying WiFi, Bluetooth, and UART functions on the CYW43455.

nodes.name: sdio_gpio_init
nodes.summary: Configures BCM2711 GPIO 34–39 to ALT3 for SlowArasan SDIO (CLK/CMD/DAT0-3) using GPFSEL3 and the BCM2711 GPIO_PUP_PDN pull-up registers.

nodes.name: sdio_fw.c
nodes.summary: CYW43455 WiFi firmware loader for Phoenix OS: reads the brcmfmac43455-sdio binary and NVRAM from the FileCore disc, downloads them to chip TCM via backplane CMD53/DMA, then releases the ARM CR4 to boot the firmware.
nodes.languageNotes: Board-aware at runtime: Pi5 uses PIO CMD53 for firmware download (BCM2835 legacy DMA absent), while BCM2711 uses DMA channel 5 (DREQ=11=EMMC). BANKPDA write is guarded by ENABLE_TCM_BANKPDA compile-time flag after bwfm analysis showed CR4 chips should not need it.

nodes.name: sdio_firmware_load
nodes.summary: Orchestrates full CYW43455 firmware download: enables func1, negotiates ALP/HT clocks, halts ARM CR4, reads firmware and NVRAM from FileCore, writes them to chip TCM via DMA or PIO, then activates the CR4 and polls for HT_AVAIL to confirm execution.

nodes.name: armcr4_activate
nodes.summary: Writes the firmware reset vector at backplane address 0, then performs bwfm-faithful ai_reset to release the ARM CR4 unhalted (CPUHALT cleared before deasserting reset), and polls HT_AVAIL to confirm firmware execution.

nodes.name: armcr4_disable
nodes.summary: Halts the CYW43455 ARM CR4 core using AI reset/IOCTL registers so TCM is AXI-accessible for firmware download while the CPU is stopped.

nodes.name: armcr4_enable_tcm
nodes.summary: Reads ARMCR4 BANKINFO for each instruction and data TCM bank to compute the real chip RAM size and optionally enables AXI access via BANKPDA; the computed size ensures NVRAM placement at the correct top-of-RAM address.

nodes.name: bp_ram_write
nodes.summary: Bulk-writes a byte array to the CYW43455 backplane RAM address using 256-byte chunked CMD53 transfers; on BCM2711 uses DMA channel 5, on Pi5 falls back to PIO CMD53.

nodes.name: dma_to_emmc
nodes.summary: Transfers a buffer to the EMMC DATA register using BCM2711 DMA channel 5 with DREQ=11 (EMMC), setting up a single control block and polling CS.END for completion.

nodes.name: d11core_reset
nodes.summary: Resets the 802.11 D11 MAC core via AI reset registers to release AXI bus locks that would otherwise stall backplane TCM access during firmware download.

nodes.name: nvram_convert
nodes.summary: Converts a raw NVRAM text file in-place to the packed CYW43455 binary format: strips comments and carriage returns, null-terminates each key=value pair, pads to 4-byte alignment, and appends the word-count token.

nodes.name: fw_read_file
nodes.summary: Reads a file from the FileCore disc by path using filecore_find_path and filecore_read_file, returning a heap-allocated buffer and size; exposed for CLM blob loading by sdio_wifi.c.

nodes.name: usb_hid.c
nodes.summary: USB HID class driver for boot-protocol keyboard and native-protocol mouse. Decodes HID reports into RISC OS keyboard_event_t/mouse_event_t and posts them to the input layer via keyboard_event()/mouse_event() from input_stub.c, completing the boot70 USB input decoupling. Also exposes hid_inject_* entry points so the Bluetooth HID path can share the same report-decode and event-posting logic.

nodes.name: usb_init.c
nodes.summary: USB subsystem initializer that sequences class driver registration (hub, HID, mass storage, keyboard, mouse) before triggering the xHCI port scan, then conditionally initializes the DWC2 OTG controller — skipping it on Pi5 where all USB is routed through RP1 xHCI.

nodes.name: usb_xhci.c
nodes.summary: Full xHCI host controller driver targeting the VL805 PCIe chip on Pi 4 and RP1 xHCI1 on Pi 5. Handles DMA ring setup (DCBAA, command ring, event ring, scratchpad), controller startup with HSE-retry logic, device enumeration, endpoint configuration, and polled control/bulk/interrupt transfers. Encodes hard-won knowledge from 94+ boot iterations diagnosing VL805 DMA coherency, ERSTBA, and command-ring sequencing issues.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses AArch64 inline assembly extensively (cntpct_el0, dsb sy, isb, AT S1E1R) for cycle-counter timing, memory barriers, and MMU page-table attribute self-checks. Dual-mode (VL805/BCM2711 vs RP1/Pi5) controlled by g_xhci_is_rp1 set at init time.

nodes.name: hid_process_keyboard
nodes.summary: Decodes a raw 8-byte HID boot-protocol keyboard report into RISC OS keyboard events: translates scan codes through ASCII/shifted tables or INKEY special-key table, applies USB modifier-to-RISC OS modifier mapping, debounces against the previous report, and posts each new key via keyboard_event().

nodes.name: hid_inject_keyboard_report
nodes.summary: Public entry point for injecting a standard 8-byte HID keyboard report from non-USB transports (e.g. Bluetooth HID). Shares the USB scan-code tables and keyboard_event() posting path with hid_process_keyboard, maintaining its own static debounce state.

nodes.name: hid_inject_mouse_report
nodes.summary: Public entry point for injecting a Bluetooth-HID mouse report into the RISC OS input queue. Auto-detects a leading report-ID byte, maps USB button bits to RISC OS SELECT/ADJUST/MENU, inverts Y axis, and calls mouse_event().

nodes.name: hid_process_mouse
nodes.summary: Decodes a native HID mouse report: auto-detects report-ID prefix on first call, reads signed delta X/Y (inverting Y for RISC OS convention), maps buttons, and calls mouse_event(). Runs once per interrupt IN transfer in hid_poll().

nodes.name: hid_poll
nodes.summary: Polls a single HID device: prefers interrupt IN endpoint (8 ms timeout for keyboard, 2 ms for mouse) and falls back to rate-limited GET_REPORT control transfer at 60 Hz if no interrupt endpoint is available. Dispatches received report bytes to hid_process_keyboard or hid_process_mouse.

nodes.name: hid_probe
nodes.summary: HID class driver probe callback: validates boot-protocol subclass, allocates hid_device_t, finds the interrupt IN endpoint, sends SET_PROTOCOL(boot) for keyboards (not mice), sends SET_IDLE to keyboards, and registers the device in the poll list.

nodes.name: hid_init
nodes.summary: Registers the HID class driver with the USB core by calling usb_register_class_driver with the static hid_driver descriptor.

nodes.name: hid_poll_all
nodes.summary: Polls all registered HID keyboards (not mice, which use hid_poll_mice). Called from the main kernel loop at approximately 16 ms intervals.

nodes.name: hid_poll_mice
nodes.summary: High-frequency non-blocking mouse poll (4 ms interval). Issues non-blocking interrupt IN transfers to drain the mouse's delta accumulator promptly, with a 500 ms watchdog fallback to a 2 ms blocking call for wireless receivers that go idle.

nodes.name: hid_device_disconnect
nodes.summary: Removes all HID poll entries for a given xHCI slot ID after disconnect. Frees each matching hid_device_t, compacts the poll array to eliminate NULL holes, and adjusts hid_device_count.

nodes.name: usb_hid_keyboard_count
nodes.summary: Returns the number of currently enumerated HID keyboards; called by CursorMod and future KeyV modules.

nodes.name: usb_hid_mouse_count
nodes.summary: Returns the number of currently enumerated HID mice/pointers.

nodes.name: usb_init
nodes.summary: Sequenced USB subsystem initializer: registers hub, HID, mass-storage, keyboard, and mouse class drivers via weak-linked calls, triggers the deferred xHCI port scan, then conditionally initializes DWC2 OTG (skipped on Pi5 where all USB goes through RP1 xHCI). Prints the block device table on completion.

nodes.name: xhci_init
nodes.summary: Top-level xHCI controller initializer: selects Pi4/Pi5 DMA buffer and offset, zero-inits the DMA region, performs MMU attribute self-check (AT S1E1R), sequences read_caps/do_reset/setup_dcbaa/setup_cmd_ring/setup_event_ring/run_controller, registers HC ops, and verifies MFINDEX post-scan. Encapsulates all VL805/RP1 hardware bring-up.

nodes.name: run_controller
nodes.summary: Programs all xHCI ring pointers into hardware (Linux order: ERSTSZ then ERSTBA then ERDP), starts the controller with RS=1, performs a 3-second HSE-retry loop until TRUE RUNNING, sends a No-op keepalive command to satisfy the VL805 MCU watchdog, powers ports, and runs a 400 ms settle loop with per-iteration ring re-arm on HSE events.

nodes.name: setup_dcbaa
nodes.summary: Allocates and initializes the Device Context Base Address Array and scratchpad pages in DMA memory. Writes DCBAA pointer to OP_DCBAAP. Includes diagnostic canary patterns (BOOT92) for MCU DMA-write verification.

nodes.name: setup_event_ring
nodes.summary: Sets up the xHCI event ring and ERST in DMA memory, computing correct DMA addresses (fixing the boot89 ERSTBA=0 bug). Also writes a fallback ERST to physical address 0 for belt-and-suspenders compatibility with early VL805 firmware behavior.

nodes.name: xhci_scan_ports
nodes.summary: Deferred port scan entry point called from usb_init() after class drivers are registered, ensuring usb_enumerate_device() can bind drivers to newly discovered devices.

nodes.name: xhci_configure_endpoints
nodes.summary: Issues xHCI Configure Endpoint commands for all bulk and interrupt-IN endpoints on a device after config descriptor parsing. Allocates per-slot transfer rings in DMA memory and stores slot_id in ep->slot_id so xhci_bulk_transfer can locate them.

nodes.name: xhci_ep_recover
nodes.summary: Recovers a halted xHCI endpoint: issues Reset Endpoint then Configure Endpoint (masked to Halted DCIs only) to restore the device to operational state without corrupting running endpoints.

nodes.name: xhci_enumerate_hub_port
nodes.summary: Enumerates a device plugged into a USB hub port: performs port reset via Set Port Feature, issues Enable Slot and Address Device commands with hub TT context, retrieves the device descriptor, and calls usb_enumerate_device().

nodes.name: xhci_enumerate_device
nodes.summary: Thin wrapper around usb_enumerate_device() that supplies the xHCI control-transfer ops; bridges the xHCI layer to the generic USB enumeration stack.

nodes.name: xhci_control_transfer
nodes.summary: Executes a USB control transfer using xHCI Setup/Data/Status TRBs on EP0 of the given device slot. Handles both IN and OUT data phases, waits for Transfer Event CCEs, and returns bytes transferred or a negative error code.

nodes.name: xhci_bulk_transfer
nodes.summary: Executes a USB bulk transfer using xHCI Normal TRBs on a pre-configured bulk endpoint. Splits large buffers across multiple TRBs, rings the endpoint doorbell, and polls for Transfer Event completion with configurable timeout.

nodes.name: xhci_interrupt_transfer
nodes.summary: Executes a USB interrupt IN transfer for HID polling. Supports timeout=0 (non-blocking event ring check), short timeout (mouse), and longer timeout (keyboard). Handles xHCI Stopped endpoint recovery (CC=13) by re-arming the TRB without resetting the endpoint.

nodes.name: xhci_irq_handler
nodes.summary: GIC interrupt handler for xHCI MSI events (INTID 180). Increments msi_fire_count for diagnostic tracking. On BCM2711/VL805 this path is non-functional (GIC delivery confirmed broken); actual event processing uses pure polling in xhci_wait_event.

nodes.name: xhci_disconnect_hub_child
nodes.summary: Handles disconnect of a device attached to a hub port: stops and disables the xHCI slot, calls hid_device_disconnect to remove HID poll entries, and frees per-slot resources.

nodes.name: xhci_check_hotplug
nodes.summary: Polls the xHCI event ring for Port Status Change Events and responds to device connect/disconnect at root hub ports. Called periodically from the kernel loop to provide hot-plug support.

nodes.name: genet.c
nodes.summary: Bare-metal BCM2711 GENETv5 GigE MAC driver for Phoenix OS (Pi 4/CM4), providing polling-mode TX/RX with direct MMIO, MDIO PHY management, cache-coherency maintenance, and transparent dispatch to the RP1 Cadence GEM driver on Pi 5.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses AArch64 inline assembly for cache maintenance (DC CVAC/CIVAC) and system counter reads (CNTPCT_EL0/CNTFRQ_EL0); all DMA buffers are statically allocated with 64-byte alignment to match Cortex-A72 cache line size.

nodes.name: genet_init
nodes.summary: Initializes the BCM2711 GENETv5 MAC: verifies hardware revision, reads board MAC address via VideoCore mailbox, configures RGMII-ID PHY mode, resets UMAC, programs MAC address, sets up DMA rings, masks interrupts, enables TX/RX, and starts PHY autonegotiation.

nodes.name: genet_apply_link
nodes.summary: Reads PHY-negotiated link speed via MDIO and programs UMAC_CMD speed field and RGMII_LINK assertion to match; must be called when physical link comes up to ungate the MAC data path and allow RDMA to advance.

nodes.name: genet_send
nodes.summary: Transmits one Ethernet frame by copying it into a static TX DMA buffer, flushing the D-cache to ensure TDMA reads actual frame data from DRAM, and advancing the TX producer index to kick the DMA engine.

nodes.name: genet_poll_rx
nodes.summary: Polls the RDMA ring for one received Ethernet frame, invalidates D-cache before reading descriptor status, copies the frame payload (skipping the 2-byte IP-alignment prefix), and advances the consumer index; always advances the ring even on error frames to prevent stalls.

nodes.name: genet_reset
nodes.summary: Soft-resets the GENET UMAC and RX/TX paths: flushes the RX buffer, issues a 200 µs UMAC core reset, clears MIB counters, sets max frame length, and programs RBUF_CTRL to the exact working value (ALIGN_2B only) discovered empirically.

nodes.name: genet_init_rings
nodes.summary: Initializes TX and RX DMA descriptor rings: disables RDMA first to avoid races with stale bootloader state, programs ring size, buffer size, start/end addresses, burst size, and populates all RX descriptor slots with static buffer addresses before enabling DMA.

nodes.name: genet_phy_init
nodes.summary: Verifies the BCM54213PE PHY is present via MDIO ID registers, issues a PHY reset, and enables autonegotiation.

nodes.name: genet_setup_rxfilter
nodes.summary: Programs the MAC destination filter with the board unicast MAC and broadcast address, then disables the MDF hardware filter (MDF_CTRL=0) and sets PROMISC mode in UMAC_CMD so all frames reach RDMA.

nodes.name: genet_link_up
nodes.summary: Returns 1 if the PHY reports link status via BMSR (read twice to clear latched-low bit); dispatches to rp1_gem_link_up on Pi 5.

nodes.name: genet_rx_available
nodes.summary: Returns the number of frames currently queued in the RDMA ring by comparing hardware producer index against the software consumer index; dispatches to rp1_gem_rx_available on Pi 5.

nodes.name: genet_delay_us
nodes.summary: Busy-waits for the specified number of microseconds using the AArch64 system counter (CNTPCT_EL0) at the hardware-reported frequency.

nodes.name: LICENSE_AUDIT.md
nodes.summary: License audit classifying all third-party code referenced or derived from in Phoenix OS into four tiers: GPL-derived conflicts (Tier 1 — nvme.c, sdio.c, sdio_fw.c), GPL-referenced rewording needed (Tier 2), permissive/MIT-compatible (Tier 3 — genet.c, bwfm), and provenance to confirm (Tier 4 — DiscReader).
nodes.languageNotes: Created at boot700 when the repo was switched to private; functions as a pre-publication checklist. Documents the decision rationale and recommended remediation order for each tier.

nodes.name: SESSION_pi5_usb_2026-06-26.md
nodes.summary: Session notes for the 2026-06-26 Pi5 USB and Bluetooth bring-up session (boots pi5-21 to pi5-38), documenting the xHCI event-ring recipe that unblocked NVMe storage, RP1 dual-xHCI topology, block-size-aware USB NVMe support, and the in-progress USB keyboard arc via usb_xhci.c on xHCI1.
nodes.languageNotes: Includes concrete next-step enumeration and suggested git commit messages, making it an actionable handoff rather than a purely retrospective record.

nodes.name: config.txt
nodes.summary: Raspberry Pi 4 / CM4 firmware boot configuration for Phoenix OS. Enables 64-bit AArch64 kernel, configures UART5 (PL011) serial console on GPIO12/13 at a fixed 48 MHz clock, forces HDMI 1080p60 output, and allocates 128 MB GPU memory for the mailbox legacy framebuffer — explicitly prohibiting KMS overlays that would break bare-metal mailbox access.
nodes.languageNotes: Raspberry Pi firmware INI-style config; section conditional [all] applies settings globally. UART5 dtoverlay replaces mini-UART to avoid core-clock-dependent baud rate corruption.

nodes.name: config-pi5.txt
nodes.summary: NEW Raspberry Pi 5 (BCM2712) firmware boot configuration for Phoenix OS first-light bring-up. Enables the BCM2712 UART0 debug serial console at 115200 (via 9.216 MHz clock) and explicitly omits Pi 4-specific settings (uart5, core_freq, KMS overlays, framebuffer) that are inapplicable or incorrect on Pi 5.
nodes.languageNotes: Pi 5 auto-loads bcm2712-rpi-5-b.dtb so no .dtb file is needed. No framebuffer support yet at Pi 5 first-light stage. Uses BCM2712 UART0 (ttyAMA0, 3-pin debug connector) rather than Pi 4's UART5 GPIO overlay.

nodes.name: XHCIInfo
nodes.summary: RISC OS loadable module implementing *USBInfo: queries the kernel's XHCI SWI provider (chunk 0x80000) to enumerate xHCI controllers, ports, and HID endpoints with live report counters, then formats and prints the result.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses Norcroft C (_kernel_oswrch, _kernel_swi_regs) for RISC OS module output rather than stdio; all output routines are hand-rolled to avoid pulling in large C library dependencies in a module context.

nodes.name: XHCIInfo
nodes.summary: Client-side header defining the XHCI SWI chunk layout (0x80000), buffer structs (xhci_ctrl_buf_t, xhci_port_buf_t, xhci_hid_buf_t), role constants, and inline static SWI wrapper functions for querying the kernel xHCI provider.
nodes.languageNotes: Buffer structs are laid out u64s-first, u32s-next, bytes-last so that natural alignment is identical under both gcc (kernel) and Norcroft (module); adding a packed attribute would silently break the kernel ABI. Pointers are cast to intptr_t because _kernel_swi_regs.r[] is 64-bit and an (int) cast would truncate the address on AArch64.

nodes.name: XHCIInfoHdr
nodes.summary: CMunge 64-bit module header descriptor registering XHCIInfo as a RISC OS module with init/final entry points and the *USBInfo command keyword.
nodes.languageNotes: CMunge processes this file through the C preprocessor before generating the module header object; apostrophes in comments must be avoided as cpp treats them as character literal delimiters.

nodes.name: Makefile
nodes.summary: RISC OS CModule Makefile for XHCIInfo, building the CMHG header object and main C object then linking via the shared CModule include; targets the gerph 64-bit Docker image with BUILD64=1.

nodes.name: VersionNum
nodes.summary: C preprocessor version-number file defining the module major/minor version (0.01) and build date for XHCIInfo.

nodes.name: README-PHOENIX.md
nodes.summary: Design rationale and reference documentation for XHCIInfo: explains why the xHCI driver stays in the kernel, why report counters matter for Pi 5 liveness checking, the full SWI interface table, build instructions, and example *USBInfo output.

nodes.name: show_controller
nodes.summary: Formats and prints a single xHCI controller's state: MMIO base, role, port count, running status, per-port PORTSC/speed/connection state, and per-HID-endpoint slot/DCI/MPS/type/arm-state/report-counter.

nodes.name: do_usbinfo
nodes.summary: Top-level *USBInfo handler: queries the controller count via XHCI_Count SWI and iterates show_controller for each, or prints a no-xHCI message on Pi 4/CM4 boards.

nodes.name: XHCIInfo_Init
nodes.summary: RISC OS module initialisation entry point registered in the CMHG header; performs no setup as this is a stateless read-only query module.

nodes.name: XHCIInfo_Final
nodes.summary: RISC OS module finalisation entry point registered in the CMHG header; performs no teardown as the module holds no resources.

nodes.name: XHCIInfo_Command
nodes.summary: RISC OS *command dispatch entry point; dispatches cmd_no 0 (*USBInfo) to do_usbinfo, following the CMHG command-keyword-table convention.

nodes.name: xhci_count
nodes.summary: Inline SWI wrapper issuing XHCI_Count (chunk+0) to the kernel; returns the number of initialised xHCI controllers, or 0 on error or Pi4/CM4 boards.

nodes.name: xhci_get_controller
nodes.summary: Inline SWI wrapper issuing XHCI_GetController (chunk+1) to fill an xhci_ctrl_buf_t with MMIO base, DMA offset, port count, role, and running state for a given controller index.

nodes.name: xhci_get_port
nodes.summary: Inline SWI wrapper issuing XHCI_GetPort (chunk+2) to fill an xhci_port_buf_t with PORTSC register value, connection, enable, and speed for a given controller/port pair.

nodes.name: xhci_get_hid
nodes.summary: Inline SWI wrapper issuing XHCI_GetHID (chunk+3) to fill an xhci_hid_buf_t with slot, DCI, MPS, live report count, and type/arm state for a given controller/HID-endpoint pair.

nodes.name: exceptions.S
nodes.summary: AArch64 exception vector table and handlers for Phoenix OS, including the #147 nesting-aware SVC stack switch in exc_sync_handler, the IRQ context-save/restore path, and UART crash-dump helpers.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses system registers TPIDRRO_EL0 and FAR_EL1 as scratch stashes to defer stack use until the SVC identity is confirmed; the 176→192 byte frame growth adds caller-SP and x18 slots at [176]/[184] to support the cross-stack return discipline.

nodes.name: exc_sync_handler
nodes.summary: EL1 synchronous exception entry point that performs an EC==0x15 check, switches to the dedicated SVC stack (or continues nested), saves the 192-byte register frame, dispatches to exc_svc_dispatch, restores caller SP before GPRs, then ERETs.

nodes.name: exc_irq_handler
nodes.summary: EL1 IRQ entry point that saves a 176-byte caller-saved register frame, calls irq_dispatch(0) in C, restores all saved registers, and ERETs to the interrupted code.

nodes.name: exc_handler
nodes.summary: Generic unexpected-exception handler that saves x0–x3, reads ESR/ELR/FAR/SP, writes them to a fixed scratchpad at 0x8F200, prints a crash banner over UART, then enters the LED blink-halt loop.

nodes.name: exc_svc.c
nodes.summary: C bridge between the assembly SVC exception handler and the kernel SWI dispatch layer; unpacks the 192-byte register frame into a uint32_t regs[10] array, calls swi_dispatch(), writes results back, and propagates RISC OS V/C flag conventions into SPSR_EL1.
nodes.languageNotes: g_svc_ceiling (uint64_t, initially 0) is the cross-file coordination point between this file and aif.c for the #147 dedicated SVC stack; 0 is treated as 'use __svc_stack_top' so BSS zero-init is correct-by-default.

nodes.name: exc_svc_dispatch
nodes.summary: SVC C bridge called from exc_sync_handler with the register frame pointer and decoded SWI number; handles OS_WriteS and OS_WriteI inline (needing ELR access), routes all other SWIs through swi_dispatch(), and sets the V/C flags in SPSR_EL1 from the return code and g_swi_carry.

nodes.name: aif.c
nodes.summary: AIF (Absolute Image Format) binary loader for RISC OS AArch64 executables; reads from FileCore, relocates into the application slot, clears BSS, manages the setjmp-style OS_Exit return context, and coordinates the #147 SVC stack ceiling discipline around aif_jump() and aif_run().
nodes.languageNotes: Uses inline asm for the setjmp/longjmp-style OS_Exit context save/restore (s_exit_buf[13]) and for the aif_jump stack switch, because GCC callee-saved registers must be controlled precisely across the AIF entry boundary.

nodes.name: aif_run
nodes.summary: Main AIF loader: looks up the executable in FileCore, validates the AIF header, copies code/data into the application slot, zeroes BSS, saves/restores g_svc_ceiling around the run, then calls aif_jump() to transfer control; handles the OS_Exit resume path.

nodes.name: aif_jump
nodes.summary: Transfers control to an AIF entry point by setting SP to the application stack then branching; lowers g_svc_ceiling to the current SP when on the SVC stack so that suspended SWI activation frames are protected during application execution.

nodes.name: aif_exit_now
nodes.summary: OS_Exit handler that restores the kernel's callee-saved registers and SP from s_exit_buf, re-enables IRQs, and branches back to the resume label in aif_run(), providing a setjmp-style non-local exit from the running AIF application.

nodes.name: gos_run_supervisor
nodes.summary: Supervisor REPL loop that reads commands and dispatches them through module_dispatch_command(), providing the interactive command interface when no AIF application is running.

nodes.name: linker.ld
nodes.summary: GNU ld linker script placing the Phoenix kernel at 0x80000 with a fixed xHCI DMA region at 0x30000000, kernel/SVC stacks after BSS, a 4KB guard gap, and a link-time ASSERT ensuring the #147 64KB SVC stack stays below the application-heap zero floor at 0x08200000.
nodes.languageNotes: Defines __svc_stack_base and __svc_stack_top as pure location-counter symbols (no output section, zero bytes in kernel8.img); the ASSERT(__svc_stack_top <= 0x08200000) is a compile-time guard for the #147 SVC stack size budget.

nodes.name: vectors.c
nodes.summary: Implements the RISC OS software vector chain mechanism for Phoenix OS, covering OS_Claim (&1F), OS_Release (&20), OS_AddToVector (&47), and OS_CallAVector (&34). Manages per-vector linked lists of claimants using a fixed node pool, with tombstone-based concurrency safety for structural edits mid-dispatch and a built-in UserV default at chain tail.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses a 64-slot static node pool (vec_node_t) with ABA-safe IDs and three calling conventions (INTERNAL/S3/CMUNGE) to interoperate with both kernel-internal handlers and 64-bit RO module veneers.

nodes.name: vectors.h
nodes.summary: Public header for the Phoenix software-vector subsystem: defines vec_handler_t (the kernel-internal claimant ABI), VEC_CLAIM/VEC_PASS/VEC_EXT_BADCONV return constants, NVECTORS and VEC_UserV, and declares all SWI back-ends and internal claim/call/release helpers.
nodes.languageNotes: Header-only: no imports, no definitions — pure type aliases, constants, and forward declarations following RISC OS naming exactly to match CMunge and RO64 conventions.

nodes.name: vec_call.S
nodes.summary: AArch64 assembly trampoline that calls external vector claimants following the VECTOR_PLAN §3 low-level convention (x0 = register-block pointer, x1 = next-dispatch address, x12 = private word), decoding the return into VEC_CLAIM/VEC_PASS/VEC_EXT_BADCONV/-1, plus two hand-written §3 test claimants used by the vector self-test.
nodes.languageNotes: Clears NZCV before the call so stale V cannot be mistaken for an error return from a CMunge 0.84 veneer; saves only x19-x22 across the blr since §3 permits x1-x15 to be corrupted by the callee.

nodes.name: vec_call
nodes.summary: Core vector dispatcher: walks the chain for vector v, invoking each live node's handler in the correct ABI (INTERNAL, §3, or CMUNGE), stopping on VEC_CLAIM and running gc_tombstones when dispatch depth returns to zero.

nodes.name: claim_node
nodes.summary: Allocates and prepends a claimant node onto vector v's chain; when dedup is set, removes all existing matching (routine, pw) pairs from the chain first to prevent duplicate entries.

nodes.name: vec_claim_internal
nodes.summary: Public entry point for kernel-internal claims: installs fn/pw as a VEC_CONV_INTERNAL claimant on vector v with optional deduplication.

nodes.name: vec_claim_s3
nodes.summary: Installs a claimant following VECTOR_PLAN §3 ABI (block-pointer convention) on vector v; used for kernel-internal §3 testing while the OS_Claim SWI path defaults to CMUNGE for real modules.

nodes.name: vec_release_internal
nodes.summary: Removes a specific (fn, pw) claimant from vector v's chain; returns the 'Bad vector release' error block (&1a1) if the pair is not found, matching the Pyromaniac expect.

nodes.name: claim_common
nodes.summary: Shared logic for both OS_Claim and OS_AddToVector SWI paths: validates vector number from regs[0] and dispatches to claim_node with the appropriate dedup flag.

nodes.name: vec_swi_release
nodes.summary: SWI back-end for OS_Release (&20): validates the vector number from the register block, then delegates to vec_release_internal, propagating the error block on over-release.

nodes.name: vec_swi_callavector
nodes.summary: SWI back-end for OS_CallAVector (&34): extracts the vector number from regs[9] and passes the register block to vec_call to run the full chain.

nodes.name: userv_default
nodes.summary: Built-in tail default handler for UserV: prints a debug message with the reason code and always passes on (returns VEC_PASS), so it only fires when nothing above it claims.

nodes.name: install_default
nodes.summary: Allocates a permanent tail node (is_default=1, never released) and appends it to a vector chain; used by vectors_init to install built-in defaults.

nodes.name: vectors_init
nodes.summary: Initialisation entry point called at boot: installs the built-in UserV default and logs the vector subsystem startup.

nodes.name: vec_selftest
nodes.summary: Comprehensive self-test exercising the full vector chain: claim/call/release lifecycles, deduplication, tombstone GC, S3 convention claimants, over-release error, and pass-on/claim ordering — mirrors the Pyromaniac expect outputs.

nodes.name: vec_econet_test
nodes.summary: Regression test replicating the *VecEconet scenario that uncovered the CMunge/§3 convention mismatch (task #138): installs CMUNGE and §3 claimants side-by-side to verify the dispatcher correctly identifies each convention.

nodes.name: vec_dump
nodes.summary: Implements the *Vectors debug command: iterates all NVECTORS chains and prints each node's vector number, routine address, private word, convention, and dead/default flags.

nodes.name: vec_dispatch_external
nodes.summary: AArch64 assembly trampoline that marshals the VECTOR_PLAN §3 entry conditions, calls an external claimant, then decodes x0/V into VEC_CLAIM (0), VEC_PASS (1), VEC_EXT_BADCONV (-2), or -1 on error (block pointer stored via err_out).

nodes.name: vec_test_external_pass
nodes.summary: Hand-written §3 test claimant that increments R1 in the register block to prove in-place block access and returns pass-on by preserving x0 (the block pointer).

nodes.name: vec_test_external_claim
nodes.summary: Hand-written §3 test claimant that increments R1, writes fingerprint 0x5A to R2, then returns claim by setting x0=0 — serves as a reference for what a correct A64 vector-claim veneer should look like.

nodes.name: module.c
nodes.summary: Core RISC OS-compatible module loader for Phoenix OS AArch64, implementing *RMLoad, *RMKill, OS_Module (SWI &1E), SWI chunk dispatch, service broadcast, CLI command dispatch, and module init sequencing with embedded binary modules and native C provider registration.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses inline assembly (module_call_with_r12) to simulate RISC OS R12 workspace-pointer calling convention on AArch64; also flushes D-cache/I-cache after relocating module code into heap-allocated memory.

nodes.name: flush_dcache_icache
nodes.summary: Flushes data and instruction caches over a given address range after relocating module code into dynamically allocated memory, ensuring coherency before first execution.

nodes.name: module_call_with_r12
nodes.summary: AArch64 trampoline that calls a RISC OS module entry point with workspace pointer in X19 (simulating ARM R12), bridging AArch64 calling convention to RISC OS module ABI.

nodes.name: module_register_native
nodes.summary: Registers a native C module (not loaded from binary) by allocating a risc_os_module_t, wiring up name, SWI base, and function pointers, then calling module_register and invoking the init callback.

nodes.name: module_register
nodes.summary: Appends a fully constructed risc_os_module_t to the global loaded-module linked list.

nodes.name: module_load_from_memory
nodes.summary: Parses and loads a RISC OS module binary from a memory buffer: validates the module header, handles both 32-bit ARM and AArch64 native variants (via init_entry bit 30 discriminator), allocates workspace and BSS, applies base relocations, and invokes the module initialisation entry point.
nodes.languageNotes: Handles the boot388 AArch64 discriminator: init_entry bit 30 set means AArch64 native; strips the flag before using the offset. Also applies ELF-style base relocations for position-independent modules.

nodes.name: module_load_from_file
nodes.summary: Loads a RISC OS module binary from a VFS path by reading the entire file into a heap buffer then delegating to module_load_from_memory.

nodes.name: swi_dispatch
nodes.summary: Dispatches a SWI number to the appropriate loaded module's SWI handler, first checking native C swi_fn, then falling back to the binary SWI handler via module_call_with_r12, and handling OS_Module built-in reasons.

nodes.name: module_broadcast_service
nodes.summary: Broadcasts a RISC OS OS_ServiceCall to every loaded module's service_fn or binary service entry, stopping early if any handler sets regs[1]=0 to claim the call.

nodes.name: module_dump_list
nodes.summary: Prints the loaded module list to the UART debug console, showing each module's name, SWI base, and base address.

nodes.name: module_dispatch_command
nodes.summary: Walks the CLI keyword table of every loaded module looking for a match to the typed command string, then invokes the matched command entry point via module_call_with_r12.

nodes.name: module_init_all
nodes.summary: Boot-time entry point that loads all built-in binary modules from their linked-in image arrays (FileCore, SDCard, FileSwitch, XHCIInfo, and others) and registers native C provider modules (SoundDMA, PhoenixDHCP, XHCIInfo), then dumps the final module list.

nodes.name: module_service_register_selftest
nodes.summary: Installs two test service handlers (SvcTest1 and SvcTest2) as native modules for in-kernel service-broadcast verification.

nodes.name: module_service_selftest
nodes.summary: Runs the in-kernel service broadcast self-test by broadcasting two service numbers and verifying handler callbacks execute as expected.

nodes.name: module.h
nodes.summary: Defines the RISC OS module header layout (PRM 1-31 with AArch64 extensions), the module instance type risc_os_module_t with native C SWI and service function pointers, and declares the complete public module management API.
nodes.languageNotes: Documents the boot388 AArch64 discriminator: init_entry bit 30 set indicates an AArch64 native module; the module_flags field (bits 4-7) provides secondary confirmation per riscos64-clib modhead.s conventions.

nodes.name: fileswitch.c
nodes.summary: Implements the RISC OS FileSwitch SWI layer for Phoenix OS, maintaining an open file handle table and routing OS_Find, OS_GBPB, OS_Args, OS_FSControl, and OS_File calls to the underlying VFS/FileCore layer.
nodes.languageNotes: File handle numbering follows RISC OS convention (1-FS_MAX_HANDLES, 0 = closed); handle slots are searched linearly with a 16-slot cap matching the RISC OS handle-count limit.

nodes.name: fs_find
nodes.summary: OS_Find implementation: opens, creates, or closes files by name or handle, selecting the appropriate FileCore or VFS backend based on path prefix and reason code, and returning a 1-based handle slot.

nodes.name: fs_bget
nodes.summary: OS_BGet single-byte read implementation: validates handle, then reads one byte from the VFS layer, returning EOF or error flags per RISC OS convention.

nodes.name: fs_bput
nodes.summary: OS_BPut single-byte write stub delegating to fs_gbpb with a one-byte buffer.

nodes.name: fs_gbpb
nodes.summary: OS_GBPB block I/O implementation: handles read/write at explicit position or current sequential pointer, routing to vfs_seek and vfs_read, and returning remaining byte count and updated position.

nodes.name: fs_args
nodes.summary: OS_Args implementation: reads and writes sequential file pointer, extent, and EOF status for open handles, delegating to vfs_seek for pointer/extent operations.

nodes.name: fs_control
nodes.summary: OS_FSControl implementation covering the most common reason codes needed for RISC OS BASIC compatibility, including catalogue, delete, and drive-selection operations.

nodes.name: fs_file
nodes.summary: OS_File whole-file operation implementation (SWI &08): handles catalogue info (reasons 5/23), load-to-address (&FF), and write-with-attributes (reasons 0/10), routing to FileCore path resolution, dr_load_object, and filecore_read_file.

nodes.name: fileswitch.h
nodes.summary: Header declaring the public FileSwitch API (fs_find, fs_gbpb, fs_bget, fs_bput, fs_args, fs_control, fs_file) with FS handle count constants and RISC OS OS_Find mode flags.

nodes.name: os_swi.c
nodes.summary: Implements the RISC OS-style SWI (Software Interrupt) dispatch table and registers seven provider chunks (BTHW 0x5A000 through XHCIInfo 0x60000), serving as the primary kernel API gateway for all OS_ calls from user space.
nodes.languageNotes: os_swi_handler spans lines 378–1564 (over 1,100 lines) — a single monolithic dispatcher using offset-based switch logic to route SWI numbers to kernel subsystems, mirroring the RISC OS OS_SWI table pattern.

nodes.name: os_swi_handler
nodes.summary: Central SWI dispatch function that routes incoming SWI offset values to the appropriate kernel subsystem (console, keyboard, mouse, memory, filesystem, modules, vectors, Bluetooth, XHCIInfo, and more).

nodes.name: os_swi_register
nodes.summary: Registers the OS SWI handler as a native module with the kernel module system, making all OS_ SWI calls dispatchable at boot.

nodes.name: gs_translate
nodes.summary: Implements GS (GlobalString) translation — processes pipe-character escapes, numeric substitutions, and OS_GSTrans-style string transformations used by the SWI handler.

nodes.name: osswi_selftest
nodes.summary: Self-test routine that exercises os_swi_handler with known SWI calls and validates responses via debug output.

nodes.name: kernel.c
nodes.summary: Main kernel boot entry point that sequentially initialises all hardware and software subsystems — MMU, IRQ, timer, scheduler, PCIe, USB, MMC, VFS, SWI table, vectors, and all seven provider chunks including the new XHCIInfo registration.
nodes.languageNotes: kernel_main is the C entry point called from AArch64 assembly startup; it ends by creating a scheduler task and calling schedule(), which never returns.

nodes.name: kernel_main
nodes.summary: Top-level kernel boot function: detects Pi model, initialises GPU/MMU/IRQ/scheduler/PCIe/USB/storage/networking, registers all SWI provider chunks, and launches the init process task before entering the scheduler.

nodes.name: init_process
nodes.summary: Post-boot init task that spawns child tasks (wimp, paint, netsurf) and then blocks, acting as the root process of the Phoenix OS task tree.

nodes.name: pci.c
nodes.summary: Full PCIe root complex driver covering Pi 4/CM4 and Pi 5 targets: link bringup, MSI programming, XHCI controller enumeration and HID/SCSI operation, keyboard/trackpad polling, and the XHCIInfo SWI provider chunk that exposes XHCI state to user space.
nodes.languageNotes: At 3,700 lines this is the largest driver in the kernel; it integrates PCIe RC bringup, full xHCI host controller logic, SCSI-over-USB mass storage, and HID input parsing all in one file.

nodes.name: pci_init
nodes.summary: Dispatches PCIe initialisation to the correct platform handler (pci_init_pi4 or pci_init_pi5) based on the detected Raspberry Pi model.

nodes.name: pci_init_pi4
nodes.summary: Brings up the Pi 4/CM4 PCIe root complex: link training, MSI setup, outbound window configuration, XHCI endpoint enumeration, and USB mass storage probing.

nodes.name: pci_pi5_rc_bringup
nodes.summary: Brings up the Pi 5 PCIe root complex controller including PHY PLL configuration, register-field programming, and link establishment.

nodes.name: pci_pi5_pcie1_bringup
nodes.summary: Brings up the Pi 5 PCIe1 port (the xHCI-bearing bus), enumerating downstream devices and setting up BAR windows for the XHCI controller.

nodes.name: pci_pi5_xhci1_run
nodes.summary: Runs the Pi 5 xHCI1 controller bring-up: reads HID report descriptors before arming the event ring (avoiding the pre-arm race), enumerates all connected HID devices (keyboard and trackpad), and arms interrupt transfers.

nodes.name: pci_pi5_xhci_run
nodes.summary: Runs the Pi 5 primary xHCI controller (xHCI0): enumerates USB mass-storage devices and issues SCSI READ(10) commands to the block device layer.

nodes.name: pci_pi5_kbd_poll
nodes.summary: Polls the Pi 5 xHCI1 keyboard and trackpad HID endpoints for new input reports and feeds keystrokes and mouse deltas to the kernel input layer.

nodes.name: xhci_controller_init
nodes.summary: Initialises an xHCI host controller from a config structure: programs DCBAA, command ring, event ring interrupter, and issues Reset and Run commands.

nodes.name: xhci_swi
nodes.summary: XHCIInfo SWI handler (provider chunk 0x60000) that exposes xHCI controller count, device slot status, port state, and HID report data to user-space callers via OS_SWI.

nodes.name: xhci_register
nodes.summary: Registers the XHCIInfo provider chunk (SWI base 0x60000) with the OS SWI dispatch table so xhci_swi becomes callable as an OS_ SWI from user space.

nodes.name: pci_pi5_kbd_enum
nodes.summary: Enumerates the Pi 5 xHCI1 keyboard and trackpad devices: reads HID report descriptors, identifies interface protocols, and sets up slot/endpoint structures for polling.

nodes.name: xhci_hid_poll
nodes.summary: Polls a single xHCI HID device's interrupt endpoint by checking the event ring for completed transfer events and returning new report data.

nodes.name: lib.c
nodes.summary: Kernel utility library providing formatted debug output, printf-family string formatting, standard C string/memory primitives, and the main UI task functions (wimp_task, paint_task, basic_task) that run as scheduled processes.
nodes.languageNotes: Combines what would normally be separate libc and task files; wimp_task at 771 lines drives the entire desktop/network/input polling loop.

nodes.name: debug_print
nodes.summary: Formatted debug output function used pervasively across the kernel — formats a printf-style string and emits it via UART and optionally the framebuffer console.

nodes.name: vsnprintf
nodes.summary: Minimal kernel vsnprintf implementation supporting %s, %d, %u, %x, %c, and %p format specifiers with width and zero-padding, used by debug_print and the sprintf family.

nodes.name: wimp_task
nodes.summary: Main desktop/windowing task that runs as a scheduled process: drives the HID polling loop, handles keyboard/trackpad/mouse input, manages TCP networking, renders framebuffer UI elements, and calls yield() to cooperate with other tasks.

nodes.name: bt_uart.c
nodes.summary: Full Bluetooth host stack driver for Phoenix OS, implementing HCI transport over PL011 (Pi4/CM4) and 16550 uarta (Pi5), with L2CAP channel management, SDP service discovery, HID device pairing/connection/polling, firmware download, link-key persistence, and a BTHW SWI provider (chunk 0x5A000) for kernel-mode BT access.
nodes.languageNotes: Board dispatch is done at runtime via get_pi_model()==5 branches in the transport helpers (bt_rx_has, bt_tx_full, bt_tx_empty) and bt_set_baud, avoiding compile-time splits. The BTHW SWI provider pattern (bthw_swi / bthw_register) follows the Phoenix module_register_native convention.

nodes.name: bt_pi5_uart_probe
nodes.summary: Probes and maps the Pi5 16550 UART (uarta @0x107D50C000) via ioremap, reads and logs UART ID/revision registers, and initialises the btu_* register accessors used by all subsequent Pi5 BT I/O.

nodes.name: bt_pi5_bt_bringup
nodes.summary: Performs the full Pi5 Bluetooth chip bring-up sequence: maps the 16550 UART, configures pin-mux, programs baud-rate divisors, sends HCI Reset, reads the BD_ADDR, downloads firmware, and re-reads BD_ADDR post-firmware.

nodes.name: bt_uart_probe
nodes.summary: Pi4/CM4 Bluetooth probe: powers on the BT chip via mailbox GPIO, initialises PL011 at 115200, sends HCI Reset, reads BD_ADDR, downloads firmware, rebauds to 3Mbps, reads BD_ADDR again, and loads saved link keys.

nodes.name: bt_download_firmware
nodes.summary: Reads the BCM43xx firmware patch file from the filesystem, streams it chunk-by-chunk to the controller via HCI vendor commands, and waits for the controller to reboot post-patch.

nodes.name: bt_set_baud
nodes.summary: Sends the BCM vendor HCI command to change the controller baud rate and then reprograms the host-side UART (PL011 or 16550) baud divisors, with a board branch on get_pi_model().

nodes.name: bt_pair
nodes.summary: Drives the classic BT SSP pairing handshake for a discovered device: sends Create Connection, handles Link Key Request, User Confirmation Request, and Simple Pairing Complete events, then saves the resulting link key.

nodes.name: bt_connect
nodes.summary: Establishes a classic BT ACL connection to a previously paired device by sending Create Connection and waiting for Connection Complete, handling authentication and role-switch events inline.

nodes.name: bt_acl_open
nodes.summary: Opens an ACL connection with optional authentication, handling Connection Request / Connection Complete / Link Key events and sending Accept Connection Request or authentication commands as needed.

nodes.name: bt_l2cap_open
nodes.summary: Sends L2CAP Connection Request for a given PSM over an ACL handle, then handles the L2CAP Connection Response and Configuration Request/Response exchange to fully open a channel.

nodes.name: bt_sdp_class
nodes.summary: Sends an SDP ServiceAttribute request for a specific service record and iterates the returned attribute list to extract and print service class UUIDs.

nodes.name: bt_sdp_search
nodes.summary: Sends an SDP ServiceSearch request to find all HID service records on the remote device and calls bt_sdp_class for each found record handle.

nodes.name: bt_l2cap
nodes.summary: High-level L2CAP setup orchestrator: opens an ACL link, opens an SDP channel, performs SDP search, then opens the HID control and interrupt L2CAP channels.

nodes.name: bt_hid
nodes.summary: Connects to a paired HID device by opening ACL and L2CAP channels (PSM 0x11 control, PSM 0x13 interrupt), then sends a HID handshake to activate report generation.

nodes.name: bt_hid_poll
nodes.summary: Polls the UART for incoming ACL/HID interrupt-channel packets and dispatches keyboard and mouse HID reports to the kernel HID injection layer.

nodes.name: bthw_swi
nodes.summary: SWI handler for BTHW chunk 0x5A000: dispatches on the SWI offset to provide bt_write, bt_read_any, bt_ms, HID keyboard injection, link-key save, and bt_hid_poll services to kernel-mode callers.

nodes.name: bthw_register
nodes.summary: Registers the BTHW SWI provider with the Phoenix kernel via module_register_native, making BT services accessible to other kernel modules via SWI chunk 0x5A000.

nodes.name: bt_inquiry
nodes.summary: Sends an HCI Inquiry command and collects Inquiry Result events to build a list of discovered Bluetooth devices, recording BD_ADDR, class-of-device, and remote device names.

nodes.name: bt_remote_name
nodes.summary: Sends HCI Remote Name Request for a discovered device and reads the Remote Name Request Complete event to retrieve the human-readable device name.

nodes.name: bt_pl011_init
nodes.summary: Initialises the PL011 UART for Bluetooth use: configures GPIO pin functions for TXD/RXD/RTS/CTS, programs baud rate divisors and FIFO/flow-control registers, and resets the UART.

nodes.name: bt_read_event
nodes.summary: Reads a complete HCI event packet from the UART with a configurable timeout, handling the HCI event header and variable-length parameter payload.

nodes.name: bt_cmd
nodes.summary: Sends an HCI command packet to the controller (waiting for TX FIFO space) and immediately reads back the resulting HCI event response with a timeout.

nodes.name: bt_scan
nodes.summary: Public entry point to run a Bluetooth device inquiry scan, enabling discoverability and delegating to bt_inquiry to collect nearby device results.

nodes.name: bt_pi5_power_probe
nodes.summary: Exported probe entry point that powers on the Pi5 Bluetooth chip using the RP1 GPIO controller sequence.

nodes.name: bt_pi5_uart_pinmux
nodes.summary: Configures the Pi5 RP1 IO_BANK pin-mux registers to route uarta TX/RX/CTS/RTS to the Bluetooth module's GPIO pins.

nodes.name: bt_acl_send
nodes.summary: Formats and sends an HCI ACL data packet with the given connection handle, L2CAP CID, and payload, used by all L2CAP channel I/O.

nodes.name: bt_write_file
nodes.summary: Persists a byte buffer to the Phoenix filesystem using filecore/dr layer calls, creating or overwriting the file at the given path.

nodes.name: bt_load_keys
nodes.summary: Reads persisted Bluetooth link keys from the filesystem into the in-memory key table on driver startup.

nodes.name: bt_pi5_power_cycle
nodes.summary: Power-cycles the Pi5 Bluetooth module by toggling the RP1 GPIO reset line with timed delays.

nodes.name: input_stub.c
nodes.summary: Input event decoupling layer providing lock-free circular queues for keyboard and mouse events; USB HID drivers post via keyboard_event()/mouse_event() and the WIMP/app layer polls via keyboard_poll()/mouse_poll() with absolute mouse position tracking.
nodes.languageNotes: Lock-free circular queue design decouples interrupt-context USB HID event producers from cooperative-scheduled WIMP consumers without requiring a mutex in the kernel's single-core boot path.

nodes.name: keyboard_event
nodes.summary: Enqueues a keyboard HID event into the lock-free circular keyboard queue for later consumption by the WIMP polling path.

nodes.name: keyboard_poll
nodes.summary: Dequeues the next pending keyboard event from the circular buffer for WIMP/application consumption; returns false when the queue is empty.

nodes.name: keyboard_inject_char
nodes.summary: Synthesizes a keyboard press event from a raw ASCII character, allowing serial or software input injection into the keyboard queue.

nodes.name: serial_kbd_poll
nodes.summary: Polls the debug UART for incoming bytes and converts them (including escape sequences for arrow and function keys) to keyboard events, bridging serial terminal input to the WIMP keyboard queue.

nodes.name: mouse_inject_move
nodes.summary: Synthesizes a relative mouse movement event from delta (dx, dy) and button state, updating absolute position and injecting into the mouse event queue.

nodes.name: mouse_event
nodes.summary: Enqueues a mouse HID event into the circular mouse queue, clamping absolute position to screen bounds and accumulating button state.

nodes.name: mouse_init
nodes.summary: Initialises the mouse event queue state and resets absolute cursor position to the centre of the default screen bounds.

nodes.name: mouse_set_bounds
nodes.summary: Sets the screen boundary rectangle used to clamp absolute mouse coordinates, called when display mode changes.

nodes.name: mouse_poll
nodes.summary: Dequeues the next pending mouse event from the circular buffer for WIMP/application consumption.

nodes.name: mouse_get_pos
nodes.summary: Returns current absolute mouse cursor position via output parameters, without consuming a queue entry.

nodes.name: mouse_get_buttons
nodes.summary: Returns the current mouse button bitmask reflecting the most recently seen HID button state.

nodes.name: keyboard_init
nodes.summary: Initialises the keyboard circular event queue and resets head/tail indices.

nodes.name: is_f3_pressed
nodes.summary: Inline predicate returning true when the keyboard event represents an F3 key press.

nodes.name: is_f12_pressed
nodes.summary: Inline predicate returning true when the keyboard event represents an F12 key press.

nodes.name: is_select_pressed
nodes.summary: Inline predicate returning true when the keyboard event is the RISC OS Select (left mouse button) equivalent key.

nodes.name: is_menu_pressed
nodes.summary: Inline predicate returning true when the keyboard event is the RISC OS Menu key.

nodes.name: is_adjust_pressed
nodes.summary: Inline predicate returning true when the keyboard event is the RISC OS Adjust (right mouse button) equivalent key.

nodes.name: uart.c
nodes.summary: Debug UART driver supporting Pi4 PL011 and Pi5 16550-compatible uart10 at 0x107D001000; provides uart_init(), uart_putc()/puts(), uart_getc(), and tx-busy query used by the kernel debug print path.
nodes.languageNotes: Runtime hardware selection via get_pi_model()/get_uart_base() avoids separate Pi4/Pi5 binaries; the Pi5 uses uart10 (not the Bluetooth uarta) to avoid firmware conflicts.

nodes.name: uart_init
nodes.summary: Initialises the debug UART: detects Pi model, selects the correct base address, configures GPIO mux for Tx/Rx pins, then programs baud-rate divisor and line-control registers for 115200 8N1.

nodes.name: uart_putc
nodes.summary: Transmits a single character over the debug UART, blocking until the TX FIFO has space; expands LF to CRLF for terminal compatibility.

nodes.name: uart_tx_busy
nodes.summary: Returns non-zero if the UART transmitter is still busy (TX FIFO not empty), used by callers that need to drain before taking action.

nodes.name: uart_drain
nodes.summary: Busy-waits until the UART transmit FIFO is fully drained, ensuring all pending debug output is committed before a halt or reboot.

nodes.name: uart_puts
nodes.summary: Transmits a null-terminated string over the debug UART by calling uart_putc() for each byte.

nodes.name: uart_getc
nodes.summary: Non-blocking receive: reads one byte from the UART RX FIFO, returning -1 if no data is available.

nodes.name: uart_set_quiet
nodes.summary: Sets a quiet flag that suppresses UART output, used to silence the debug console during sensitive operations.

nodes.name: sdio_wifi.c
nodes.summary: CYW43455 WiFi driver implementing the full SDPCM/BCDC protocol stack: firmware bring-up, CLM blob loading, WPA2 association via sdio_wifi_join(), DHCP negotiation, and Ethernet frame Tx/Rx bridging to the kernel network layer.
nodes.languageNotes: The SDPCM (Software Defined Protocol for Channel Management) and BCDC (Broadcom D11 Control) protocols are proprietary Broadcom interfaces layered over raw SDIO CMD52/CMD53 register reads and writes; the CLM (Country Locale Matrix) blob must be loaded after firmware to configure regulatory domains.

nodes.name: sdio_wifi_init
nodes.summary: Top-level WiFi initialisation sequence: locates SDPCM command registers, waits for firmware readiness, enables SDIO function 2, joins the configured network, and kicks off DHCP.

nodes.name: wifi_join
nodes.summary: Full WPA2 association sequence: loads CLM blob, configures country/band/channel, sets event mask, issues join IOVAR with SSID and WPA2 credentials, then polls for CONNECT or DISCONNECT events with timeout.

nodes.name: bcdc_iovar
nodes.summary: Core BCDC IOVAR transport: marshals a get or set command into an SDPCM/BCDC packet, writes it via CMD53, then polls for the matching response frame with retry and event-drain logic.

nodes.name: wifi_wait_fwready
nodes.summary: Polls SDIO bus state and firmware console output until the CYW43455 firmware signals readiness, then configures SDPCM bus credits and interrupt enables.

nodes.name: wifi_poll_rx
nodes.summary: Polls the SDIO function 2 receive path for a pending frame, validates the SDPCM header, strips protocol overhead, and returns the inner Ethernet payload to the caller.

nodes.name: wifi_dhcp_run
nodes.summary: Runs the DHCP client state machine after association: configures the send/target callbacks, starts the DHCP exchange, polls rx frames until an IP lease is bound or timeout occurs.

nodes.name: wifi_dump_fw_console
nodes.summary: Reads the CYW43455 firmware's in-memory ring-buffer console log via backplane reads and prints it to the debug UART for bring-up diagnostics.

nodes.name: sdpcm_rx_frame
nodes.summary: Receives a single SDPCM frame from the CYW43455 via CMD53 with a configurable timeout, returning the raw SDPCM buffer to the caller.

nodes.name: wifi_clm_load
nodes.summary: Loads the CLM regulatory blob from the filesystem into the CYW43455 firmware using chunked IOVAR writes, required before any association attempt.

nodes.name: wifi_send_ethernet
nodes.summary: Wraps a raw Ethernet frame in an SDPCM/BDC header and transmits it to the CYW43455 via CMD53 for over-the-air delivery.

nodes.name: wifictl_swi
nodes.summary: SWI (software interrupt) dispatch handler for the WiFi control module, routing kernel module calls to the appropriate WiFi operation.

nodes.name: wifictl_register
nodes.summary: Registers the WiFi control module with the kernel module registry, making it accessible via the SWI dispatch table.

nodes.name: wifi_net_poll
nodes.summary: Polls for a received WiFi Ethernet frame and passes it to the kernel network Rx handler; called from the main scheduler loop.

nodes.name: wifi_find_sdregs
nodes.summary: Discovers CYW43455 internal register addresses (chip ID, SB regs) by probing the backplane at known offsets, logging results to debug UART.

nodes.name: wifi_enable_func2
nodes.summary: Enables SDIO function 2 (the WiFi data path) on the CYW43455, waiting for the function-ready bit and configuring block size.

nodes.name: resolver_module.c
nodes.summary: Implements the DNS resolver as a RISC OS-style module and SWI provider, wrapping a raw UDP DNS query engine (packet builder, response parser, AArch64 timer helpers) behind init/final/swi entry points so other RISC OS modules can resolve hostnames via a SWI call.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses inline ARM64 MRS instructions (cntpct_el0, cntfrq_el0) for timing; implements a minimal DNS UDP client from scratch rather than relying on a libc resolver.

nodes.name: res_putip
nodes.summary: Formats a 32-bit IPv4 address as a dotted-decimal string and prints it to the UART debug output.

nodes.name: parse_dotted_decimal
nodes.summary: Parses a dotted-decimal IPv4 address string into a 32-bit packed integer, returning false on malformed input.

nodes.name: build_dns_query
nodes.summary: Constructs a DNS A-record query packet in wire format for a given hostname, writing it into a caller-supplied buffer with the specified transaction ID.

nodes.name: parse_dns_response
nodes.summary: Parses a raw DNS response packet, validates the transaction ID and answer section, and extracts the first A-record IPv4 address into the output parameter.

nodes.name: resolver_module_init
nodes.summary: RISC OS module initialisation entry point; performs a test DNS lookup at startup and prints the resolved address to UART, demonstrating the resolver is operational.

nodes.name: resolver_module_final
nodes.summary: RISC OS module finalisation entry point; logs a shutdown message via UART.

nodes.name: resolver_module_swi
nodes.summary: RISC OS SWI handler dispatching on swi_offset; SWI 0 (Resolver_GetHostByName) copies the hostname from register r0, calls the kernel DNS resolver, and returns the IPv4 address in r1.

nodes.name: roconform.py
nodes.summary: CLI conformance-checking tool for Phoenix OS sources that validates RISC OS module structure and provider-pattern compliance by running two sub-commands: vectest (parses captured test output against expected oracles) and diff (text diffing against expected output files).

nodes.name: Check
nodes.summary: Accumulates pass/fail boolean results and prints a summary report of how many checks passed and failed.

nodes.name: check_vectest
nodes.summary: Validates captured vectest output against oracle expectation files, checking section structure, RISC OS vector call naming, error numbers, SWI numbers, and handler addresses using regex matching.

nodes.name: check_diff
nodes.summary: Compares a named section of captured output text against a stored expected file, printing pass/fail with diff context.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: CLI entry point; parses arguments for the vectest and diff sub-commands, reads the captured input file, validates the expect directory, and dispatches to the appropriate check function, exiting non-zero on failure.

nodes.name: README.md
nodes.summary: Documents the roconform.py Phoenix OS conformance checker, covering the two checking levels (vectest — operational, and diff — stubbed/blocked), command-line usage examples, and known limitations.

nodes.name: EXC_IRQ_STACK_PLAN.md
nodes.summary: Design specification for making exc_irq_handler safe to enter from application context (#126), recommending a contained SP-swap to a dedicated IRQ stack (Approach A, ~30 lines in exceptions.S) and deferring the full SP_EL0/SP_EL1 split (Approach B) with a documented 8-item brick-path checklist for when multi-core forces it. Lays out three implementation stages: S1 safe stack, S2 unmask IRQs for apps, S3 FP/SIMD save and IRQ-driven consumers.
nodes.languageNotes: Covers AArch64 EL1h/EL1t stack-pointer semantics, DAIF masking, TPIDR_EL1 use for per-core save areas, and the -mgeneral-regs-only constraint that defers FP/SIMD save to S3.

nodes.name: MODULAR_ARCHITECTURE.md
nodes.summary: Architecture direction document establishing the target shape of Phoenix OS as a lean board-agnostic kernel core plus runtime-loadable RISC OS modules from the boot disc, preserving the one-binary property. Defines the hard chicken-and-egg boundary between what must stay in-kernel (boot storage stack, MMU, scheduler, provider registrations) and what can become a loadable module, and documents the provider/client SWI-chunk mechanism, ABI versioning gaps, failure modes, and open questions for the riscos64 maintainer.
nodes.languageNotes: References the OS_ClaimOSSWI collusion mechanism, 32-bit reg-block constraint on the SWI path (uint32_t regs[10]), and the DT-HAL runtime board-detection strategy that keeps PI_MODEL compile-time defines out of source.

nodes.name: MODULE_ADOPTION_PLAN.md
nodes.summary: Operational adoption plan for integrating up to 52 prebuilt AArch64 RISC OS 64 modules from riscos64-status/rm64/ into Phoenix, organised into five priority batches. Records live boot-test findings: FileTypes hangs due to missing OS_BGet carry channel and ResourceFS; FSCommands, OSCommands, BootLog, and SystemBell load cleanly; KernelIntrospection installs OS_ReadSysInfo and OS_PlatformFeatures via OS_ClaimOSSWI; and the command layer is proven end-to-end with OS_GSTrans identified as the highest-leverage remaining gap.
nodes.languageNotes: Distinguishes SWI chunk &0 modules (no SWIs, lowest conflict risk) from modules with own chunks; tracks the OS_BGet carry-flag return-channel gap as a foundational fix needed before further module adoption.

nodes.name: MULTICORE_PLAN.md
nodes.summary: Detailed multi-core (SMP) implementation plan for Phoenix OS adopting an asymmetric compute offload strategy (lane A) rather than full SMP. Covers 6 staged milestones from single-core groundwork through waking secondary cores via SEV/WFE, per-core EL1 stacks and spinlocks, IPI round-trip, offload primitive, and all-four-cores support — with board-difference matrix for Pi 4 vs Pi 5 and open questions for the RISC OS author.
nodes.languageNotes: 19 sections across 496 lines. References issue #126 (exc_irq_handler / proper EL1 stacks) as the primary gate for secondary-core bring-up. Tracks both Pi 4 and Pi 5 paths throughout staged milestones.

nodes.name: VECTOR_PLAN.md
nodes.summary: Design document (v4) for Phoenix OS's RISC OS-compatible software vector subsystem, specifying Claim/Release/CallAVector/AddToVector semantics, per-vector chain structure, tombstone model for safe mid-dispatch edits, and the external module veneer (deferred). Includes evidence-cited open questions for the RISC OS author and acceptance criteria tied to Pyromaniac test expectations.
nodes.languageNotes: 15 sections across 544 lines with a v4 revision history. Distinguishes KNOWN design facts from OPEN questions for the external RISC OS expert (Charles). References SVC vs IRQ context differences and a first-proof target of UserV.

nodes.name: HANDOFF.md
nodes.summary: Root-level engineering handoff document summarizing the current state of Phoenix OS for new contributors, including what was completed in the latest arc (native PCIe NVMe SAVE), the next session's starting point, hardware setup, memory map, SWI implementation status, key source files, and a rolling changelog of recent boot sessions.
nodes.languageNotes: 36 sections across 435 lines covering boot sessions boot516 through boot599a. Tracks progress by boot-counter numbers (e.g., boot520, boot577) which serve as build/session identifiers. Complements docs/HANDOFF.md as the root-level copy.

nodes.name: README.md
nodes.summary: Primary project README for Phoenix OS, documenting the RISC OS-inspired bare-metal AArch64 kernel's milestone history (from boot143 through current), current feature set, hardware targets (CM4/Pi4/Pi5), USB architecture, DMA layout, FileCore and xHCI key lessons, build instructions, serial console setup, and key file index.
nodes.languageNotes: 41 sections across 973 lines. Uses milestone sections (🎉 Boot NNN) as the primary narrative structure, each describing a discrete achieved capability. The most recent milestone covers software vectors and real RISC OS module interoperability.

nodes.name: HANDOFF.md
nodes.summary: Rolling per-session engineering handoff log for Phoenix OS, with entries spanning boot33 through boot102b, covering Pi 5 bring-up (xHCI, PCIe NVMe, WiFi, Bluetooth, CrowView trackpad), CM4 USB split transactions, module system development, software vectors implementation, and the latest software-vector ABI measurement and chunk-bug findings.
nodes.languageNotes: 58 sections across 1261 lines — the most detailed file in this batch. Uses H1 headings per session and H2/H3 for subsections. The final session (2026-07-17, boot101-102b) documents ABI measurement results (#138), a chunk bug (#139), and next steps for the software vector subsystem.

nodes.name: Makefile
nodes.summary: Top-level GNU Makefile for Phoenix OS that compiles and links a bare-metal AArch64 kernel targeting Raspberry Pi 4 (cortex-a72) and Pi 5 (cortex-a76), assembling roughly 90 object files from kernel, drivers, net, wimp, and apps subsystems into a flat binary image. Updated for issue #147 to include the SVC stack (exc_svc.c), software vector dispatch (vectors.c, vec_call.S), XHCIInfo provider, and the DNS resolver module (resolver_module.c), with a cross-compilation toolchain using aarch64-linux-gnu-gcc in -ffreestanding -nostdlib mode.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses GCC to assemble .S files (instead of bare 'as') so that C pre-processor macros and the 'ldr x0,=symbol' pseudo-instruction both work in assembly sources. DiscReader objects receive an extra -U_FORTIFY_SOURCE flag to suppress glibc fortification wrappers that have no counterpart in a -nostdlib binary. An explicit dependency rule for kernel/test_module.o captures the .incbin'd PhoenixTest.bin file, which Make's generic pattern rule cannot see.

nodes.name: all
nodes.summary: Default phony target that builds the final phoenix64.img binary image.

nodes.name: kernel.elf
nodes.summary: Links all compiled object files via kernel/linker.ld to produce the kernel ELF, which is then stripped to a flat binary by the phoenix64.img rule.

nodes.name: clean
nodes.summary: Removes all compiled object files and build artefacts (kernel.elf, phoenix64.img).

nodes.name: help
nodes.summary: Prints usage instructions for BOARD selection and available make targets.

nodes.name: Development Journal
nodes.summary: Running development log (boot572-99+) tracing Phoenix OS through Pi5 complete (boot69-75a), then #147 dedicated SVC stack (boot76-99): root cause = exc_sync_handler ran every SWI on interrupted 2KB GOS stack; *Modules dispatch ~2.7KB overran into CLI buffer corrupting clisize. Fix: nesting-aware switch to 64KB SVC stack in exceptions.S (x9 in TPIDRRO_EL0, caller SP in FAR_EL1, bounds-compare vs __svc_stack_base/__svc_stack_top); g_svc_ceiling in exc_svc.c; aif.c ceiling save/lower/restore for BASIC; ASSERT in linker.ld. Verified Pi4 AND Pi5: *Echo after *Modules INTACT, *BASIC→run→QUIT→*Echo INTACT. Journal also covers XHCIInfo provider (SWI 0x60000, *USBInfo command for xHCI controller status including Pi5 trackpad report counters), RISC OS software vectors (OS_Claim/OS_Release/OS_CallAVector — task #129, boot99, tombstone model), and new planning docs (EXC_IRQ_STACK_PLAN, MODULAR_ARCHITECTURE, MODULE_ADOPTION_PLAN, MULTICORE_PLAN, VECTOR_PLAN). Key lesson: to force rebuild touch ONLY *.c/*.S sources — NEVER touch *.o (makes objects newer than sources, skips recompilation).

edges.description: Path-based pairing (deterministic)
xHCI driver depends on PCIe RC + VL805 initialization in pci.c
VL805 xHCI development encompassed the multi-boot ERSTBA cache investigation
xHCI driver development culminated in the event ring fix at boot 143
xHCI driver depends on the DMA buffer layout for ring pointers and context memory
xHCI driver implements the USB enumeration stack (Enable Slot, Address Device, GET_DESCRIPTOR)
USB mass storage depends on the enumeration stack to identify and address the NVMe device
USB mass storage (RTL9210 NVMe bridge) is the block device backing FileCore/ADFS disc access
FileCore/ADFS provides disc access for loading RISC OS module binaries (.ffa files)
Module Init() calls RISC OS SWIs — requires SWI dispatch infrastructure to be in place first
AArch64 RISC OS modules use riscos64-clib for their C runtime (_clib_initialisemodule)
CursorModule is a key kernel-linked AArch64 RISC OS module in the module system
The module system registers ARM32 modules as stubs pending AArch32 EL0 mode switching
