GENETv5 driver is the hardware layer underlying the Phoenix network stack
The event ring fix at boot 143 was enabled by analysing Circle's xHCI driver object files
SWI dispatch provides OS services that modules call during Init() and operation
The ERSTBA cache problem led to relocating ERST to physical address 0 and changing DMA_OFFSET to 0
Rules 1-50+ document VL805/xHCI-specific hardware behaviour and correct sequences
Rules 47-57 document GENET, RGMII, ARP, and network driver best practices
Rules 118-120 document SDIO SlowArasan controller addressing and bus power requirements
DWC2 EP0 control transfer pattern informed xHCI GET_DESCRIPTOR fix
WIMP task polls GENET RX ring and drives the network receive path every 4ms tick
WIMP desktop uses CursorModule for mouse pointer rendering and input management
Boot 35 (controller running), boot 118 (DWC2 device), boot 143 (event ring) are xHCI milestones
Boot 314 (first frames on wire) and boot 340 (reliable ping) are GENET milestones
usb_bdev_read calls bot_recover on transfer failure then retries
usb_mass_storage_init registers usb_storage_probe as the class driver probe callback
usb_mass_storage.c depends on blockdriver.h for blockdev_t/blockdev_register and xhci functions via extern declarations
usb_mass_storage_init indirectly configures the blockdev ops table containing usb_bdev_read
Paired blockdev read/write ops on the same storage drive
timer_tick and timer_irq_handler are both timer firing paths; timer_irq_handler is the GIC ISR, timer_tick is the software callback walker

project.name: Phoenix OS
project.description: Bare-metal AArch64 OS for Raspberry Pi 4/CM4/Pi5, RISC OS-inspired. ~30k lines C and Assembly. Pi5 complete: NVMe PCIe + Cadence GEM + CYW43455 WiFi + BT keyboard live on single kernel8.img. #147: dedicated 64KB SVC stack (nesting-aware SP switch, g_svc_ceiling, aif ceiling). Software vectors: OS_Claim/OS_Release/OS_CallAVector (task #129, tombstone model). 7-module provider suite complete: BTUart/WiFiCtl/BoardInfo/HALInfo/DiscInfo/Ifconfig/XHCIInfo (0x5A000-0x60000).

layers.name: Boot & Early Initialization
layers.description: AArch64 boot stub, EL2→EL1 transition, Pi5 timer EL2 fix (cnthctl_el2/cntvoff_el2), BSS zeroing, MMU setup, periph_base two-sample CLO detection

layers.name: Kernel Core Services
layers.description: Scheduler, IRQ controller (GIC-400 Pi4/Pi5), memory allocator, inter-process primitives, board info cache, get_pi_model()

layers.name: Device Tree / FDT
layers.description: Flattened Device Tree parsing (volatile byte reads to defeat -O2 load-merging), peripheral detection, board-specific addressing; CM4 boots with no DTB (dt_valid=0)

layers.name: OS SWI & Module System
layers.description: Exception vectors (exceptions.S), SVC stack nesting (#147: 64KB dedicated SVC stack, g_svc_ceiling, aif_jump ceiling save/restore), SWI dispatch (exc_svc.c, os_swi.c), software vectors (OS_Claim/OS_Release/OS_CallAVector/OS_AddToVector, vec_call.S tombstone model, task #129), FileSwitch, RISC OS module loader, provider chunk table (0x5A000-0x60000: BTUart/WiFiCtl/BoardInfo/HALInfo/DiscInfo/Ifconfig/XHCIInfo)

layers.name: Filesystem & Storage
layers.description: RISC OS FileCore, DiscReader (ADFS new-map, 4K-native NVMe), FileSwitch, VFS, AIF loader

layers.name: Hardware Drivers

tour.title: Project Overview
tour.description: README.md is the definitive entry point to Phoenix OS: a RISC OS-inspired bare-metal AArch64 kernel for Raspberry Pi 4/CM4/Pi 5 built in ~29k lines of C and Assembly. It catalogues 23 sections covering milestone boot numbers, hardware architecture, USB and FileCore design, DMA layout, and key source file references. docs/ARCHITECTURE.md follows with the design philosophy and the AArch64 physical memory map, while README_BOOT.md gives the practical startup checklist a newcomer will observe on the serial console.
tour.languageLesson: Milestone boot numbers (e.g. Boot 143, Boot 543) appear throughout this codebase as breadcrumbs in comments and the engineering journal — each number marks a session where a major capability first worked. They provide a development timeline you can cross-reference against docs/journal.txt.

tour.title: Build System & Memory Map
tour.description: The Makefile drives aarch64-linux-gnu- cross-compilation of all C and Assembly sources into kernel.elf, while config.txt configures the Raspberry Pi GPU firmware: 64-bit kernel8.img, UART serial console, HDMI forced at 1080p60, and 128 MB GPU memory without KMS overlays that would break the bare-metal mailbox framebuffer. The linker script kernel/linker.ld places the kernel at physical 0x80000, defines the .xhci_dma DMA-coherent section at a fixed address, and exports the __bss_start/__stack_top symbols consumed by the boot stub.
tour.languageLesson: Raspberry Pi config.txt is parsed by the VideoCore GPU firmware before the ARM cores start — it is not a Linux config file. arm_64bit=1 tells the GPU to load kernel8.img instead of kernel7.img and start the primary ARM core in AArch64 EL2. Setting gpu_mem=128 reserves 128 MB at the top of RAM for the GPU heap; the kernel must not write into this region or the mailbox framebuffer negotiation will corrupt GPU state.

tour.title: AArch64 Boot Stub
tour.description: kernel/boot.S is the very first code that executes after the Pi 4 firmware hands control to kernel8.img. The _start symbol parks secondary CPUs via MPIDR_EL1, drops the exception level from EL2 to EL1 by writing ELR_EL2/SPSR_EL2 and executing ERET, sets the kernel stack pointer, installs the VBAR_EL1 exception vector table, zeroes BSS, and branches to kernel_main. Understanding this file shows why the kernel can safely assume EL1 and a valid stack by the time any C code runs.
tour.languageLesson: AArch64 position-independent address loads use ADRP (page-relative) + ADD (offset) rather than a 64-bit immediate because the linker cannot know the physical load address at link time. The EL2→EL1 transition is atomic: writing ELR_EL2 sets the return PC, writing SPSR_EL2 sets PSTATE at EL1 (M=0b0101 = EL1h), and then ERET switches both simultaneously.

tour.title: Exception Vectors & SVC Dispatch
tour.description: kernel/exceptions.S installs the VBAR_EL1 exception vector table — 128-byte-aligned slots for every AArch64 exception type and source EL. Synchronous exceptions (SVC instructions) are routed to exc_sync_handler, which performs a nesting-aware switch to the dedicated 64KB SVC stack (#147): it saves the caller's SP into FAR_EL1, compares against __svc_stack_base/__svc_stack_top bounds, and switches SP only when not already on the SVC stack. g_svc_ceiling in exc_svc.c holds the current ceiling pointer (0 = use __svc_stack_top). aif_jump() lowers the ceiling before launching a BASIC app from inside a SWI so the suspended SWI activation's frames survive; aif_run() restores it on OS_Exit. This replaced the interrupted 2KB GOS stack that *Modules was overrunning (~2.7KB deep) into the CLI buffer. exc_svc_dispatch() unpacks saved x0–x9 into a uint32_t regs[10] array, calls swi_dispatch(), propagates the result to SPSR_EL1 V/C flags (boot421: V set on error, C set for OS_BGet EOF/OS_GSTrans overflow via g_swi_carry), then ERET restores the (possibly modified) registers. OS_WriteS and OS_WriteI are handled pre-dispatch (need direct ELR_EL1 access). Verified Pi4 AND Pi5: *Echo after *Modules INTACT, *BASIC→run→QUIT→*Echo INTACT.
tour.languageLesson: ARMv8 requires each vector slot to be exactly 128 bytes wide (32 instructions), enforced by .align 7 in the assembly source. Phoenix includes a boot599 sanity guard on the SVC path that checks ELR_EL1 for obviously-corrupted values before ERET — a lesson learned from smashed stack frames that caused phantom instruction-fetch faults deep in the xHCI driver.

tour.title: kernel_main: The Boot Script
tour.description: kernel_main() is the C entry point from the AArch64 boot stub. It orchestrates a 9-stage boot sequence: (1) detect_peripheral_base() reads the DTB for MMIO addresses; (2) wdog_disable() kills the BCM2711 watchdog; (3) uart_init() starts the mini-UART console; (4) gpu_init() + board_info_init() — board_info caches serial number, MAC, board model, and revision from the VideoCore mailbox so all drivers can query them without mailbox overhead; (5-9) MMU, IRQ/timers, block/net/filesystem init, module_init_all(), bt_uart_probe(), then task_create("init") and schedule().

tour.title: FDT, Peripheral Detection & MMU
tour.description: kernel/periph_base.c probes for the peripheral base address at boot using a two-sample CLO delta to distinguish a live timer from stale SDRAM content — critical for reliable Pi4/Pi5 discrimination. kernel/devicetree.c parses the FDT using volatile uint8_t* byte reads throughout to defeat -O2 load-merging that caused pre-MMU alignment faults. CM4 still passes no DTB (dt_valid=0 → all dt_get_* return 0 → fallback to hardcoded BCM2711 constants); Pi4 gets a real DTB; Pi5 has its own DT-aware addressing. kernel/mmu.c builds the identity page table. Pi5 NVMe PCIe window added (boot65-68): l1_table[110] = L1_DEVICE(0x1B80000000) device-maps the Pi5 pcie1 outbound window (DT pcie1 ranges: CPU 0x1B80000000 → PCIe 0x80000000). Also maps RP1 window (l1_table[124], 0x1F00000000) for RP1 GEM Ethernet and Pi5 xHCI.
tour.languageLesson: FDT integers are big-endian regardless of host byte order — on a little-endian AArch64 core every property field must be byte-swapped before use. Phoenix implements be32() manually since there is no libc. AArch64 MAIR_EL1 defines up to eight memory-attribute index slots; Phoenix uses index 0 = Normal WB (RAM), index 1 = Device-nGnRnE (MMIO), index 2 = Normal Non-Cacheable (DMA bounce buffers). Getting these wrong causes silent data corruption on DMA.

tour.title: Interrupt Controller & Scheduler
tour.description: kernel/irq.c initialises the BCM2711 GIC-400 (GICv2) interrupt controller — distributor (GICD) and per-CPU interface (GICC) — and maintains irq_table[256] for driver-registered handlers. kernel/sched.c builds a 4-CPU symmetric round-robin scheduler on top, with per-CPU run queues, spinlock-protected enqueue/dequeue, assembly-level context_switch (saving AArch64 callee-saved registers), and cross-CPU wakeups via GICv2 SGIs. The ARM Generic Timer in kernel/timer.c fires at 250 Hz via PPI-30, calling timer_tick which drives schedule().
tour.languageLesson: GICv2 has two MMIO blocks: the Distributor (GICD, shared, configures interrupt routing) and the CPU Interface (GICC, per-CPU, handles ack/EOI). Software-Generated Interrupts (SGIs, IDs 0–15) are triggered by writing GICD_SGIR with a target CPU bitmask — Phoenix uses SGI-0 as its IPI to wake a remote CPU when a task is enqueued on it.

tour.title: PCIe, xHCI USB & HID Input Decouple
tour.description: kernel/pci.c is a unified PCIe RC driver for Pi4/CM4/Pi5 in one binary. Pi4/CM4: BCM2711 PCIe RC (pcie0) → VL805 xHCI (USB) via EXT_CFG; CM4 also does NVMe endpoint. Pi5 pcie0: BCM2712 RC → RP1 southbridge (built-in xHCI0 + GEM). Pi5 pcie1 (boot65-68): RC at 0x1B000000000 → NVMe M.2 Samsung 970 EVO Plus. Bus-number routing fix: must set bridge primary=0/secondary=1/subordinate=1 + mem window + MEM|MASTER command BEFORE downstream config reads — without secondary=1 all config reads return 0xffffffff (UR). Outbound window: CPU 0x1B80000000 → PCIe 0x80000000; NVMe BAR0 = PCIe 0x80000000. Boot70 USB HID decouple: pci_pi5_xhci_run() had storage-first coupling — grabbed first connected xHCI port as "the NVMe", bailed if not MSC. Fix: storage_ok flag + hid: label — "not a disc" exits fall through to HID enum (dport=-1 lets keyboard claim even on the probed port). USB keyboard+mouse now work with or without USB storage.
tour.languageLesson: xHCI uses producer/consumer TRB ring buffers. The cycle bit (C) in each TRB indicates ownership: the host flips C when submitting and the controller echoes the flipped bit in completion events to prevent ABA races. A Link TRB at ring-end with Toggle Cycle makes the ring logically circular. The DMA region must sit in a Normal Non-Cacheable MAIR slot — reading it without DC IVAC after a controller write returns stale cached data.

tour.title: Block Devices: SD, NVMe, USB MSC & Disc Registry
tour.description: blockdriver.c abstracts storage: SD (MMC/EXT_CSD), NVMe (IDENTIFY), USB MSC. DiscReader bridges block devices to FileCore. DiscInfo provider (SWI chunk 0x5E000, boot684): discinfo_swi in filecore.c exposes the multi-disc registry to the *Discs RISC OS module (DiscInfo-phoenix). Key lesson: do NOT trust the on-disc FileCore DiscRecord for geometry — a cloned disc carries the SOURCE DiscRecord (CM4 eMMC cloned from 500GB NVMe showed "4096/465GB" in DiscRecord). Fix: report physical geometry from the blockdev struct (bd->size * bd->block_size, bd->block_size, bd->name) which comes from hardware (EXT_CSD/NVMe IDENTIFY) and is immune to clone staleness. *Discs output: "NVMe 4096/465GB, eMMC 512/~15GB/emmc".

tour.title: FileCore Filesystem & VFS
tour.description: FileCore implements the RISC OS ADFS filesystem. The DiscReader subsystem (DiscReader.h, dr_init.c, DirUtils.c, Directories.c, DiscOps.c) translates physical ADFS new-map disc structures into an in-memory representation. DiscOps.c was the key fix for 4K-native NVMe: its ReadSectors function now handles 4096-byte physical sector translation, enabling all 14 disc modules to load from the Crucial P3 NVMe. FileCore then provides the VFS path resolution, file I/O, and SWI dispatch consumed by FileSwitch above.
tour.languageLesson: FileCore 'New Map' format stores the disc allocation bitmap in zones, each covering a contiguous LBA range. A file's data is located by an IDA (Indirect Disc Address) chain across zones. Phoenix resolves IDA → LBA by finding the object in the zone bitmap and applying LFAU (Logical File Access Unit) arithmetic — a process that must correctly handle cross-zone fragments and the special Obey-script meta-entries in directories.

tour.title: RISC OS Module System, SWI Dispatch & Provider Pattern
tour.description: os_swi.c (~1160 lines) is the SWI dispatch hub: a mega-switch handling 30+ OS_ SWIs and a CLI (*-command) sub-dispatcher. module.c is the module manager: module_load_from_memory() allocates a PAGE-aligned owned copy of the module image with ZI zeroed and appended, flushes D/I cache, then calls the AIF Init routine at the module's entry point. The Provider Pattern (boot676-687): kernel registers a SWI chunk handler for OS data (BTHW/WiFiCtl/BoardInfo/HALInfo/DiscInfo/Ifconfig/XHCIInfo at 0x5A000-0x60000); a RISC OS module reads that data via _kernel_swi using a shared struct that is byte-identical between gcc kernel and Norcroft RISC OS compiler. Software Vectors (task #129, boot99): OS_Claim(&1F)/OS_Release(&20)/OS_AddToVector(&47)/OS_CallAVector(&34) implement RISC OS per-vector chains. Each vector slot holds a singly-linked list of claim_node structs (owner + handler address). vec_call.S provides vec_dispatch_external — the AArch64 trampoline that calls each Thumb2/ARM module handler in turn and short-circuits when a handler claims the vector. Tombstone model for mid-dispatch edits: a released node is zeroed in place and skipped by the walker, so the chain stays consistent during traversal. vec_selftest() and vec_econet_test() exercise the full claim/release/callavector round-trip at boot.
tour.languageLesson: RISC OS modules are self-contained shared-library + driver units identified by a 36-byte header. Word offsets 0–8 are pointers (relative to the header) to the module's entry points; a zero means that entry is absent. The workspace pointer (R12) is unique per module-instance and is set up by module_call_with_r12 before every call into the module — this is how modules maintain private state without global variables.

tour.title: Networking: Multi-Interface Stack (GENET + RP1 GEM + WiFi)
tour.description: Phoenix runs a multi-interface IP stack on Pi4/CM4/Pi5. Pi4/CM4: GENET (net/genet.c) drives the BCM2711 GigE MAC directly. Pi5: RP1 GEM (drivers/net/rp1_gem.c) drives the Cadence GEM inside the RP1 southbridge — same BCM54213 PHY family, but GEM MMIO at 0x1F00100000, DMA offset +64GB (RP1 masters: CPU_phys + 0x1_0000_0000 → PCIe addr). CYW43455 WiFi: Pi4 uses SlowArasan SDIO host (sdio.c); Pi5 uses RP1 SDHCI brcmstb (sdhci_brcmstb.c, MMIO 0x1001100000) — standard SDHCI spec vs the proprietary host. Both interfaces share net/ ARP, DHCP, DNS, TCP. Ifconfig provider (SWI chunk 0x5F000, boot687): ifconfig_swi/ifconfig_register in net/dhcp.c fills ifcfg_buf_t for each interface. *Ifconfig RISC OS module reads via ifconfig_count()/ifconfig_get(i). HW result: GEM/GENET up 192.168.0.110 + WiFi up 192.168.0.112, both with mask/gw. Pi5 complete: wired + WiFi + BT all live.

tour.title: GPU Framebuffer, Input Events & WIMP Event Loop
tour.description: GPU framebuffer (drivers/gpu/framebuffer.c) is initialized via VideoCore mailbox. Pi5 note: VC returns 16bpp RGB565 even when 32bpp is requested — depth is derived from the mailbox-returned pitch, not the requested depth. drivers/input/input_stub.c (boot70, new): decoupled input event layer. Provides keyboard_event()/mouse_event() for USB HID to post into, and keyboard_poll()/mouse_poll() for WIMP/apps to consume. Lock-free single-consumer circular queues (KBD_QUEUE_SIZE=16, MOUSE_QUEUE_SIZE=16). Mouse absolute position tracked with dx/dy accumulation and screen-bounds clamping via mouse_set_bounds(). Previously USB HID posted directly to WIMP — the decoupling enables the Pi5 USB HID decouple fix (keyboard works whether or not a USB disk is present). bt_print() → con_printf() → framebuffer mirror: useful when serial console drops bytes during rapid BT firmware download (photograph the screen to read results).

tour.title: AIF Loader & BBC BASIC
tour.description: When the user invokes BBC BASIC, basic_task in kernel/lib.c calls aif_run in kernel/aif.c. aif_run resolves the path through FileCore, reads the AIF binary, validates the header (read-only size, read-write size, BSS size, relocation flag), allocates the application memory slot, copies code and data, zeroes BSS, applies self-relocation, then branches to the entry point via the aif_jump naked trampoline. BBC BASIC then issues RISC OS SWIs (OS_File, OS_GBPB, OS_WriteC, OS_ReadLine, etc.) that flow through the exception-vector → exc_svc_dispatch → os_swi_handler → fileswitch chain built in the earlier steps.
tour.languageLesson: AIF (ARM Image Format) is the RISC OS self-relocating binary format. The first 128 bytes are a fixed header encoding image sizes and the relocation flag. When the relocation flag is set the image contains a self-relocation stub as the first code that runs: it patches all absolute addresses relative to the current load address before jumping to the real entry point. Phoenix's aif_exit_now uses a longjmp to unwind back to wimp_task on OS_Exit without unwinding across the EL0/EL1 boundary.

tour.title: Engineering Journal, Pi 5 Complete & Session Notes
tour.description: docs/journal.txt (7000+ lines, boot572-99+) is the authoritative source of Phoenix OS boot history. boot65-68: Pi5 NVMe PCIe — pcie1 RC, bus-number routing fix (primary=0/secondary=1/subordinate=1 required before config reads), board-aware DMA offset (Pi5 0x10_00000000 vs BCM2711 0xC0000000), Samsung 970 EVO Plus registered as blockdev unit 1. boot69-75a: Pi5 BT complete (16550 uarta, four-stage bring-up, board-aware helpers), CrowView USB keyboard + trackpad live, USB-input decouple (storage_ok / hid: label). boot76-99: #147 dedicated SVC stack (exc_sync_handler nesting switch, 64KB SVC stack, g_svc_ceiling, aif ceiling); *Echo after *Modules INTACT, *BASIC→run→QUIT→*Echo INTACT verified Pi4+Pi5. boot99: XHCIInfo (SWI 0x60000, *USBInfo — 7th provider) + software vectors (OS_Claim/OS_Release/OS_CallAVector, vec_call.S, tombstone model). Journal also covers: RP1 GEM Cadence GEM Ethernet (Pi5), sdhci_brcmstb.c WiFi SDIO host, input_stub.c decoupled event layer, license audit. Five planning docs added: EXC_IRQ_STACK_PLAN (dedicated IRQ stack roadmap), MODULAR_ARCHITECTURE (provider-module pattern reference), MODULE_ADOPTION_PLAN (remaining kernel→module migrations), MULTICORE_PLAN (SMP roadmap), VECTOR_PLAN (software vector expansion roadmap). Key build lesson: touch only *.c/*.S to force rebuild — NEVER touch *.o (makes objects newer than sources, silently skips recompilation).

tour.title: Bluetooth: Pi5 BT Complete (16550 Transport + Board-Aware Stack)
tour.description: bt_uart.c implements the full BT host stack (HCI→L2CAP→SDP→HID) plus BTHW provider (SWI chunk 0x5A000). Pi4/CM4 uses PL011 UART for BT. Pi5 uses a completely different transport: "uarta" 16550/8250-style UART @0x107D50C000 (BCM2712). Pi5 bring-up (four stages, boot71-75a): (1) bt_pi5_power_probe() — drives BCM2712 gio GPIO 29 high to power CYW43455 BT core. (2) bt_pi5_uart_probe() — maps uarta, reads regs (divisor=0, fsel=0 → must configure). (3) bt_pi5_bt_bringup() — muxes gpio24-27 via BCM2712 pinctrl @0x107D504100 (RTS=3, CTS=4, TXD=4, RXD=4), configures 16550 at 115200 8N1, HCI Reset → "04 0e 04 01 03 0c 00" — BT alive. Same milestone as CM4 boot661. (4) bt_download_firmware() + boot75a — 323-record .hcd unchanged (same chip), real BD_ADDR, BT keyboard live: *BTScan → *BTPair → bonded → auto-HID → L2CAP psm=0x13 → "HID LIVE". Board-aware transport helpers: bt_rx_has()/bt_tx_full()/bt_tx_empty() branch on get_pi_model()==5 → read 16550 LSR (DR b0, THRE b5, TEMT b6 @offset 0x14) else PL011 FR. All higher-level BT functions (bt_inquiry, bt_pair, bt_acl_send, etc.) use these helpers unchanged. Pi5 console is uart10 @0x107D001000 — a SEPARATE UART — so BT bring-up never touches the debug console. L2CAP pending fix (boot685): on result=0x0001 PENDING → keep looping (not break). BTUart-phoenix RISC OS module: full portable host stack over BTHW SWIs.

tour.title: RISC OS Provider Modules: Complete Suite (0x5A000-0x60000)
tour.description: Seven RISC OS provider modules (boot676-99) implement the kernel/module split: kernel owns hardware/data, portable module reads via _kernel_swi. The shared struct is byte-identical between gcc kernel and Norcroft RISC OS compiler so the same header compiles both sides. BTUart (0x5A000): full BT host stack — *BTScan/*BTPair/*BTConnect/*BTL2CAP/*BTHID. WiFiCtl (0x5B000): *WiFiStatus — SSID/IP/MAC from wifi_info_t. BoardInfo (0x5C000): *BoardInfo — model/revision/RAM/serial. HALInfo (0x5D000): *HALInfo — GPIO/MMIO base addresses, Pi variant. DiscInfo (0x5E000): *Discs — registered block devices (unit, size, type). Ifconfig (0x5F000): *Ifconfig — per-interface IP/MAC/flags. XHCIInfo (0x60000): *USBInfo — xHCI controller count, port states, HID endpoint report counters (including Pi5 trackpad X+Y); implemented via xhci_count/xhci_get_controller/xhci_get_port/xhci_get_hid in the shared header; do_usbinfo() + show_controller() in the RISC OS module side. All modules follow the same CMHG-generated header, Init/Final/Command entry points, and ROM module table structure.
